release.description: Search your Telegram Business archive, read what a voice message said, and reply — through a hosted MCP server.

interface.short_description: Your Telegram, in ChatGPT
interface.long_description:
Lemma Telepath connects your Telegram Business account to ChatGPT so your assistant can work with your own business conversations. Ask it to summarise a thread, find the message where a price or a deadline was agreed, read a screenshot a client sent, listen to a voice message as text, or draft and send a reply as you.

It is built on the official Telegram Business API: you add our bot as your Business chatbot in Telegram and grant it the rights you choose, so there is no MTProto user session and nothing is scraped. From that moment your 1:1 business messages are archived into an account that is yours alone — one isolated database per account, full-text searchable, including the text inside attachments and transcripts of voice and round-video messages.

You stay in control of what the assistant may do. Every capability — replies, media, notes, group archiving — is a switch you can turn off at any time from the bot, and sending is surfaced for your confirmation before anything reaches another person. You can erase everything you have stored with a single command.

Telepath is not end-to-end encrypted and we say so plainly: searching and transcribing require our servers to read your messages. Data is encrypted at rest with full-disk encryption, each account is physically isolated, and voice transcription is opt-in, disclosing the processor it uses before you turn it on. If you need a guarantee that no operator can ever read your data, the same connector can be self-hosted on your own machine.

release.description: Gives any spreadsheet a brain: studies the data with code, asks only what the data can't answer, writes what it learned into a tab inside the file (a file next to a CSV), keeps it current, and draws a map of what connects to what.

interface.short_description: Give any spreadsheet a brain
interface.long_description:
Sheet Geek gives a spreadsheet a brain: notes about what the data means, saved with the file.

It reads every row of an .xlsx, .xlsm or .csv file with code, tells you in a few lines what the sheet is and what stands out, and asks only the handful of questions the data cannot answer: your goal, what a number really means, what to leave out. It saves what it learned as a _brain tab in the workbook (in ChatGPT, in a copy you download; for a CSV, in a .brain.json file next to it): what each column means, how tabs and files connect, what you said and what code counted, each note labeled and dated. An AI that opens the file later and reads its tabs can start from those notes. It can also draw a clickable map of how the data connects, flag notes that went stale when the data changed, and write a data dictionary, a guide for the next owner or an app blueprint.

For anyone whose spreadsheet other people, or their AI tools, need to understand: finance models, purchasing logs, client trackers, inventories.

Limits: it never changes your data cells. Notes kept on "this machine only" stay in a .sheet-geek folder on your computer; in ChatGPT they last only as long as the chat. Password-protected files and old .xls files are not supported, and it is not for health records, payment card data, government ID numbers or passwords. The code makes no network calls, never starts another program and never searches the web. Each brain's first note ends with one line naming Sheet Geek and Actual Intelligence Labs.

Open source (Apache-2.0) by Actual Intelligence Labs.

interface.short_description: Openings, puzzles, game facts
interface.long_description:
Chessigma answers chess questions with its opening guides, an opening catalogue and facts computed from the rules of chess. Ask about the London, the Caro-Kann, the Sicilian and 15 more openings to get the main line, the key variations and the ideas for both sides from Chessigma's opening guides, or name any of 3,700 catalogued lines to get its ECO code and moves. Also: the daily puzzle with its solution, and Elo estimates with FIDE, Chess.com or Lichess K-factor defaults (Chess.com and Lichess use Glicko ratings, so their real changes differ). No account needed.

For chess players of any level who want facts about openings, positions and games. Chessigma does not evaluate positions inside ChatGPT, does not play games, and cannot read your Chess.com or Lichess account: share a game link or a PGN instead.

release.description: An AI-aware design system, read from the code you already have: your coding agent writes each page the way your other pages are built

interface.short_description: Pages built like your others
interface.long_description: UI Consistency makes your project's own design system something the coding agent reads before it writes UI. Ask for a page, a form or a change to one, and the agent first reads how the pages you already have are built: which shared components they use and how, the theme and its tokens, how they validate input and show errors. Then it writes the new page the same way, from a checklist, and has a separate agent compare the result with the page it follows. It works with any UI technology, including plain HTML and CSS, in a single app or a monorepo, and needs no configuration. It reads only your project; it has no server, no network access and no telemetry, and writes nothing into your repository besides the pages you asked for. It needs a project with code to read: in a conversation without one there is nothing for it to follow.

release.description: Discover publisher RSS feeds, sitemaps, cached health and first-discovered article-URL activity.

interface.short_description: Find RSS feeds and sitemaps
interface.long_description:
Find configured publisher RSS feeds and sitemaps across countries for source research, feed setup, and news monitoring projects.

Search by publisher name or domain, country, endpoint type, category, language, and configuration status. View source details, browse supported countries, and inspect separate RSS and sitemap health records with actual check times, parsed item or URL counts, sample URLs, and publication-date information when available.

Health is cached from bounded operator checks. Check times are separate from content dates: a reachable feed may contain old content, and a cached result may become stale. Some configured endpoints are empty, blocked, unavailable, malformed, or could not be fully checked. Country and configuration counts do not represent unique publishers or guaranteed live coverage. Sitemap indexes describe child sitemap entries; child files and article links are not validated by this plugin.

Read active source-registration inventory and cached first-discovered unique article-candidate URL activity by source or country. Country counts deduplicate across sources. Every new endpoint/source binding begins with an excluded baseline; untracked periods return null, and partial initialization or collection is explicit. Calendar days use a requested IANA timezone or UTC; rolling 24 hours is separate. Activity queries read retained aggregate history in bounded ranges of up to 31 calendar days per request. Older stored dates remain queryable; periods before real recording are not reconstructed. These counts are discoveries, not publications or feed entry counts. Homepage/section/forum heuristics are separated; sitemap-index children are excluded. No semantic content deduplication is performed.

World News Sources provides read-only source metadata and observation aggregates. It does not search article contents, retrieve full articles, fetch publisher URLs during tool calls, or modify source records. No account or API key is required to use its public MCP endpoint.

For support, contact myungeun2dc@gmail.com.

release.description: LLM, text-to-speech and speech-to-text for voice agents and AI agents: set Hopper up in a voice-agent project, measure time to first token on its own prompt, find what slows it down, and speak or transcribe audio.

interface.short_description: Voice AI inference for agents
interface.long_description: Hopper serves open-source models for real-time voice agents: a low-latency LLM behind a standard chat-completions API, plus text-to-speech and speech-to-text. Hopper speaks text with an inline audio player, transcribes recordings you attach (WAV, MP3, M4A, Ogg, FLAC or WebM) with word timestamps, lists models and prices, returns tested integration code for popular voice-agent frameworks, and reviews a voice agent's prompt, tools and client code for what delays its first reply. After you sign in with your Hopper account, it shows your usage and creates API keys. Where it can run commands in your project, the plugin also sets Hopper up in a voice-agent codebase: it measures time to first token on the agent's own system prompt and tools in a 10-turn simulated call and shows the results before changing any code, and after you say go it switches only the LLM. Text and audio you send go to Hopper's API; see withhopper.com/privacy.

release.description: Amazon product research, keyword research, and seller data: live demand, pricing, competition, ASIN, offer, and listing insights for Amazon sellers.

interface.short_description: Amazon keyword & seller data
interface.long_description:
Amazon product research, keyword research, and seller data inside ChatGPT. Ask in plain language and get live Amazon marketplace data to validate product ideas, size demand, and study the competition before you source or launch.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
- Validate a product idea: Amazon search volume, keyword difficulty, search-interest trends, pricing across marketplaces, and competition level.
- Amazon keyword research: expand a seed keyword into related search terms with monthly search volume, cost-per-click, ranking challenge, and a seasonal trend; compare search volume for up to 1,000 keywords at once to shortlist ideas.
- Reverse ASIN lookup: see every keyword an Amazon listing ranks for, its rank positions, and a position-bucket summary.
- Amazon competitor analysis: find the products that genuinely compete with a listing, plus brand concentration, market share, and top sellers.
- Amazon seller data: look up a third-party seller's public storefront profile, feedback percentages, and the products they sell.
- Amazon listing and Buy Box data: current price, availability, rating, review count, category path, best-seller rank, feature bullets, and every seller offer with condition, Prime eligibility, and FBA or FBM fulfillment.
- Amazon search results: run a live Amazon search for a keyword and review every listing on the page, including purchase signals such as the "bought in past month" badge.
- Browse product categories to find new niches and ideas.

BUILT FOR
Amazon sellers, FBA and private-label brands, wholesale and arbitrage sellers, dropshippers, and e-commerce entrepreneurs who want data-backed answers to questions like: Is there demand for this product? Who are the top sellers? How hard is it to rank? What keywords does this ASIN rank for? How contested is the Buy Box?

HOW IT WORKS
The plugin queries live Amazon marketplace and search data when you ask, so answers reflect current listings, prices, and search demand. Sign in with your 1Product account to connect. The plugin only researches: it never lists, edits, or buys anything on Amazon and does not publish content on your behalf. When data is unavailable it says so plainly instead of guessing.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon.com, Inc.

release.description:
New CV Tool connects a user-controlled career profile and application workspace to ChatGPT. After sign-in, ChatGPT can read approved career evidence and job-search criteria, save found opportunities, create tailored CV and cover-letter drafts, and refine the document the user is working on. It can also compare applications, select templates, adjust supported formatting, measure actual PDF layout, and keep the application board organized.

The connector is designed around factual restraint: it must not invent employers, dates, qualifications, titles, or results. It never sends an email, submits an application, or treats a board-status change as proof that an employer was contacted. Users review and export final documents themselves in New CV Tool.

Structured profile and workspace records remain in CV Tool Cloud. A separate Google consent flow is optional and is used for document-file storage and generated exports. Access is owner-scoped through OAuth, and users can disconnect the connector or delete their data from New CV Tool.

release.description:
Fiveable for AP Teachers connects your Fiveable teacher workspace to ChatGPT for AP grading, class materials, assignments, and insights.

Grade a stack of AP free responses. Paste student work in chat or import PDF and Word files on Fiveable, including AP Classroom "By Student Page Break" exports. Direct file uploads depend on the ChatGPT surface you use. Fiveable scores supported AP question types using their AP rubrics and point totals. Review the rubric, adjust individual part scores with a reason, and approve responses one at a time or together. AI scores stay labeled as drafts until you approve them.

Make tomorrow's class materials. Find questions from Fiveable's AP question bank with their stimuli, answer keys, and explanations. Ask ChatGPT to arrange them into a warm-up, exit ticket, worksheet, or review game, with a separate answer key and Fiveable attribution.

Build and run assignments. Set up classes, add a roster, and build drafts from Fiveable multiple-choice questions, free responses, study guides, and guided notes. Drafts stay invisible to students. Publishing, changing publication dates, and releasing results each show a preview and wait for your confirmation. Editing scores or feedback after results are released can change what students see.

See where each class needs support. Review class and student results, answer-choice breakdowns, and topics or skills that need more practice. Ask ChatGPT to use those results to draft a reteaching plan, parent note, or conference outline. When a class has no scored work, Fiveable reports that limitation.

With Google connected on Fiveable, list Classroom turn-ins, export grading results to a Google Sheet, and preview sending approved numeric AP scores to Classroom. Classroom documents can be imported on the Fiveable website. Sending scores does not send written feedback or return the work; you return it in Classroom yourself.

Student identifiers in tool results are minimized to short display names and opaque handles. Structured results omit student emails and account IDs. Full response text is returned only when explicitly requested. Work you paste or upload may contain identifying information, so remove unnecessary personal details before sharing it.

interface.short_description: Safety verdicts on AI agents
interface.long_description:
Ask whether an AI agent, MCP server, coding assistant or AI product is safe to use, and get a straight verdict from Greenlit Books, with the setup steps that make it safer and a link to the full review. Each verdict comes from reading the product's own code, docs and settings, and says which version it read and when. There are more than 800 of them, covering coding assistants, automation tools and hundreds of MCP servers.

It also checks statements about AI agents against a ledger of 564 claims, each sorted by what it rests on (a published result, the book's argument, a method you can run, or the author's own account) and each with a citation. Where a claim rests on an outside source, the result says what that source does and does not establish.

Ask it how or why about working with AI agents and it answers from Greenlit's books: it finds the passage in the free first chapters, the concept pages, the glossary and the claim ledger that bears on your question, quotes it with a link to the exact section, and points you to the page where the rest of the topic is. And when you want to go deeper, it finds the right practical book on working with AI, with a free first chapter to read.

Read-only. No account and no sign-in. Nothing you ask is stored beyond short-lived request logs.

release.description: Optician exam calculators for the ABO and NCLE, with every step shown.

interface.short_description: Optician exam calculators
interface.long_description:
Opterio works the optics math on the ABO and NCLE optician exams, one step at a time. Ask about a prescription or a frame and Opterio runs the calculation, shows every step, points out the trap the exam likes to set, and rounds to the nearest quarter diopter where that matters.

Twelve calculators:

- Transposition: move a prescription between plus- and minus-cylinder form.
- Spherical equivalent: sphere plus half the cylinder, naming both quarter steps when the result lands halfway.
- Vertex distance: compensate a prescription for a change in vertex distance, one meridian at a time, for example from glasses to contact lenses.
- Prentice's rule: induced prism and its base direction when the eye looks away from the optical center, for spheres and sphero-cylinders.
- Lens thickness: edge or center thickness from power, index and diameter, compared across common lens materials.
- Minimum blank size: the smallest lens blank a frame needs, from its effective diameter, eye size, bridge and the patient's PD.
- Base curve: Vogel's estimate of the front curve for a prescription, halving the spherical equivalent first for a minus lens.
- Lens power: the power from the front and back curves, with back vertex power for a thick lens and lens clock readings converted for the material.
- Prism resolver: horizontal and vertical prism combined into one resultant prism in 360-degree notation, or one prism split back into its parts.
- RGP fitting: a GP contact lens power from the K readings, the glasses prescription and the base curve, with the tear lens and any residual astigmatism.
- Near PD: the reading PD from the distance PD and the reading distance, with the three-quarter rule.
- Effective diameter: twice the longest radius from the boxing center, or an estimate from the frame box and how rounded the corners are.

Every answer comes with a card that shows the result and the working. Open it full screen to change any number and watch the answer update, see the diagram, and try an exam-style practice problem. Answers come in English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Tagalog, Vietnamese or Korean, following the language you write in.

Opterio is for study and for checking your own working. It isn't a prescribing tool and doesn't replace a clinician's judgment.

There's no account to create, and the calculators don't save what you enter.

release.description:
Need help doing something? 

Ask any question and get clear, simple, step-by-step instructions.

This guide helps you learn almost anything, from everyday jobs to hobbies, school projects, cooking, fixing things, technology, travel, crafts, and much more. 

Tell it what you want to do, and it will explain each step in order. No confusing words. No long walls of text. Just easy directions you can follow.

You can ask big questions or small ones. Want to bake a cake? Change a bike tire? Tie a tie? Clean your keyboard? Learn chess? Start a garden? Build a website? Pack for a trip? The guide breaks every task into small, simple steps that are easy to understand. If you get stuck, ask another question and keep going.

Every guide is made just for you. Tell the guide if you are a beginner, a child, a student, or someone with lots of experience. Say what tools you have, how much time you have, or what you already know. The instructions will change to match your needs.

Hard jobs become easier when they are split into small pieces. Each step builds on the one before it, so you always know what to do next. If something needs extra care, the guide points it out. If there is a better or faster way, it can explain that too. You can even ask why a step matters.

Ask follow-up questions at any time. If one step is confusing, ask for a simpler explanation. Need more detail? Want fewer steps? Prefer a checklist instead? Want tips for beginners? The guide can change the answer without making you start over.

Use it at home, at school, at work, or while traveling. It can help with cooking, cleaning, crafts, gardening, pets, fitness, computers, phones, writing, studying, art, music, games, photography, organization, home projects, and many other topics. If there is a task with clear steps, this guide can usually help explain it.

The guide can also help you compare different ways to do something. Ask which method is easier, faster, cheaper, or better for beginners. If a job needs special tools or materials, you’ll learn what you need before you start. If there are common mistakes, you’ll learn how to avoid them.

release.description:
Nerra gives ChatGPT and the rest of your AI tools the same up-to-date picture of your company knowledge. Connect Slack, Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, Jira and your meeting notes once. Nerra reads them, picks out what matters (decisions, customers, owners, current plans) and keeps it current as things change.

For example, your support AI agent can’t answer a customer's question, so it escalates it to a teammate. Once they reply, Nerra saves as knowledge, and next time your AI agents knows it.
Nerra brings the right company context into your ChatGPT conversation, whatever the topic. Ask about a customer and you get their recent emails, meetings and deal status. Ask about a feature and you get the decisions, the discussion behind them and who's responsible.

You can also ask ChatGPT to save something new. Nerra saves it along with who said it and when. After that, every AI tool connected to Nerra knows it.

What you get:
Your agents work from validated and current knowledge, so fewer answers rely on outdated docs
One memory for every AI tool your team uses
The current version of each fact, plus how it changed and why
Answers about your company with a quote and a source link
Saved notes your team can see, check and correct

Built for teams that use several AI tools and agents and keep copying the same context from one to another.

release.description:
Hyperus OEE connects ChatGPT to Hyperus, the industrial IoT platform that monitors production machines in real time. Ask questions about your factory in plain language and get answers backed by the same data you see in the Hyperus OEE dashboard.

What you can ask:
- Real time: which machines are running or stopped right now, why, and since when; a machine's timeline for the shift or the day; stops still waiting for a justification.
- OEE: OEE, availability, performance, and quality for any period up to one year, compared with the previous period, plus trends by day, week, or month.
- Stops: Pareto of stop reasons, breakdown into sub-reasons, and individual occurrences with operator notes.
- Production: production by product and by hour, production orders and their performance, product search.
- Maintenance: MTBF, MTTR, and failure indicators by machine.
- Quality and people: SPC summary and operator performance, for users with those permissions.
- IoT: sensor telemetry such as temperature, pressure, and energy.

Read-only and secure: the app never changes anything in Hyperus. You sign in with your own Hyperus account (including your company's MFA policy) and see only the machines, devices, and data you already have access to. Access changes made in the dashboard take effect within 60 seconds, and you or an administrator can revoke the connection at any time from the Hyperus dashboard.

Requires an active Hyperus OEE account.

release.description: Design and read advertising incrementality tests: platform lift studies, geo experiments, switchbacks and directional pre/post checks, with a bundled, validated analysis script.

interface.short_description: Incrementality tests for ads
interface.long_description:
Measure whether your ads drive results that would not have happened anyway.

Fiera Incrementality helps paid media teams choose the right test, design it, and read it:

- Planner: turns a question (is brand search incremental? should we cut Meta prospecting?) into a test plan. Recommends the platform's own lift study when one is available, a geo experiment when channels must be compared on business data, and a switchback or a directional before/after read when nothing else is possible.
- Geo test design: from a CSV of KPI by region and day, picks treated regions by stratified randomization, estimates the minimum detectable effect on held-out history, the test length and the cost, and writes a plan to approve before launch.
- Geo test readout: estimates the effect with two methods (time-based regression and synthetic control), intervals from placebo tests, incremental CPA and ROAS, and robustness checks.
- Quick incrementality: a directional read on a pause or budget change, compared with several baselines and their normal noise, plus switchback analysis for single markets.
- Lift result review: an independent check of a lift study, vendor test or internal claim.

Results feed attribution (incrementality factors) and marketing mix models (Meridian, Robyn, PyMC-Marketing) as calibration. Methods follow the published work behind Google's TBR and Meridian GeoX, Meta's GeoLift and the synthetic control literature, with sources cited in the skills.

The analysis runs in a bundled Python script on the data you upload. It is calibrated on simulated panels: false positive rate in A/A tests, coverage of the true effect, and power at the predicted detectable effect.

Intended for performance marketing, growth and analytics teams. Limits: results are as good as the KPI data you provide; directional methods are labeled as such and do not prove causation; platform lift studies are run in the ad platform, not by this plugin.

release.description: Reports what business and first class actually cost on US domestic routes, using the US Department of Transportation's Airline Origin and Destination Survey (DB1B). Answers two questions: what a premium seat costs on a given route, and which routes a given budget can reach. Distinguishes lie-flat beds from recliners so a cheaper seat is not mistaken for a better one.

interface.short_description: How much is the good seat?
interface.long_description:
You were going to spend $300 on a seat at the back. On that route, on that date, the flat bed might be closer than you think — or far further away. Flying Fine tells you which.

Ask what business or first class costs on any of 1,503 US domestic routes and you get the real range: the cheapest fare recorded, the typical fare, and the high end — drawn from actual tickets sold, published quarterly by the US Department of Transportation. Give it a budget instead and it will show you which routes that money can actually reach, longest trip first.

It also separates lie-flat beds from reclining seats. On some routes the cheapest premium ticket is a recliner while a genuine flat bed costs a few hundred more, and price alone will not tell you which is which.

These are historical figures, not live fares, and the plugin says so every time. Where a route rests on only a few dozen recorded tickets it flags that too, rather than presenting a thin number as a firm one. There is no booking and no checkout — you confirm with the airline.

interface.long_description:
Home finds homes for sale and to rent across the United Kingdom from home.co.uk, right in the conversation. Describe what you want in your own words: a town, city or postcode, buying or renting, your budget, how many bedrooms, new build or not, newest or lowest price first, and what you want in the home itself, such as a garden, off-road parking, a quiet street, period features, open-plan living, a home office or no onward chain. Open any result for the full picture in chat: every photo, the complete description, the agent, key facts and, where the published address can be matched to a property, checks from Homedata such as the EPC energy rating, council tax band, flood and other environmental risks, broadband, nearby schools and recorded crime. Keep a shortlist and compare two to four homes side by side. See which homes are within a walk, cycle or drive of a station, office, school or postcode, and put up to six viewings in the quickest driving order for the day. Ask what an area is like for schools, broadband, recorded crime and local house price growth, see recent sold prices and typical rents nearby, find local estate and letting agents, and estimate stamp duty or monthly mortgage repayments from your own figures.

Home also brings five workflows: what can I afford, turning a monthly budget and deposit into a price and the homes at it; prepare for a viewing, with a checklist and questions for the agent built from the home's own details; plan a viewing day, with the order, the driving between stops and what to ask at each; shortlist and compare, ranking homes against what matters to you, commute included; and buying costs, setting out stamp duty, deposit, loan and monthly repayments together.

It is for anyone house hunting: first-time buyers, movers, renters and families comparing places to live. Searching, viewing property details, comparing homes and using the planning and calculator tools need no account.

Limitations: Home does not value homes or forecast prices, list a home, contact agents for you, or decide mortgage eligibility. Kalori is a nutrition catalog for Japanese convenience stores and restaurant chains. It covers 380+ chains (Seven-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart, Saizeriya, Sukiya, McDonald's Japan and more) and returns calories and protein, fat, and carbohydrates for their items. Data is refreshed nightly from official chain sources, and every item carries a nutritionSource marker: official means the chain publishes the value, partial means published values completed with AI estimates, and estimated means every value is AI-estimated.

Search terms, filters, and result counts are retained as the linked account's search history to improve catalog coverage; each call also records the IP address and user-agent in private operational logs that are deleted automatically after about seven days. The tools accept no precise location, chat transcripts, or third-party account identifiers, and personal records are only ever reached through the user's own linked account.

interface.short_description: Service reliability, in chat
interface.long_description:
Nobl9 is the reliability platform, built on service level objectives (SLOs) and error budgets. It tells you whether the services your customers depend on are working, how much room you have before they notice a problem, and what to fix first. With this app, you can ask ChatGPT those questions in plain words and get answers from your own live Nobl9 data, in the same conversation where you do the rest of your work.

Ask things like: Which of my services are closest to burning their error budget this month? What reliability target should the payments API have, given how it has behaved? Which alerts fired this week and which ones mattered? Set up a target for this service, and show me before you change anything.

What you get: a straight answer on service health in one question; the story behind an alert, with the data that fired it; reliability targets built from how your services behave for users, with the error budget tracked against real monitoring data; alerts that page when a budget is burning fast and stay quiet when it drifts slowly; a status update you can paste into a channel, written from the numbers.

Nobl9 works from the monitoring tools your team already runs, including Prometheus, Datadog, Dynatrace, New Relic, Amazon CloudWatch, Google Cloud Monitoring, Splunk and others, so there is nothing new to instrument and the answers match your dashboards.

What it can do: read your services, SLOs, error budgets, alerts and connected data sources; run a query against a connected data source; and draft, validate or apply an SLO or alert policy when you ask.

How it stays safe: you sign in with your own Nobl9 account, and ChatGPT sees only what you can see. Asking questions never changes anything. When you ask it to set up or change a target or an alert, it drafts the change, validates it against your organization, and shows you the full definition.

Intended for developers, data engineers, and platform teams who automate Preset or Apache Superset with HTTP requests, curl, or Python.

Limitations: the skills assume a Preset API token is available in the execution environment, and they act only on teams and workspaces that token can already reach. They do not bundle credentials, and they do not create Preset accounts or handle billing.

interface.short_description: Plan and instrument analytics
interface.long_description:
Accoil Product Tracking is a set of seven skills for engineers and product teams who need reliable product analytics in a B2B SaaS codebase.

What it does:
- Model the product: scan the codebase and ask a few questions to describe users, accounts, entities, and how value flows (.telemetry/product.md).
- Audit current tracking: inventory existing analytics SDK calls, identity handling, and event naming (.telemetry/current-state.yaml).
- Design a tracking plan: propose a minimal, consistently named set of events, properties, and group hierarchy, plus a delta from the current state (.telemetry/tracking-plan.yaml, .telemetry/delta.md).
- Generate an implementation guide for one of 25 destinations, such as Segment, Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog, RudderStack, Google Analytics, Sentry, LaunchDarkly, or a generic HTTP API (.telemetry/instrument.md).
- Implement tracking: generate typed wrapper functions and identity management code in a tracking/ directory.
- Instrument new features: update the plan, delta, and changelog when a feature ships, changes, or is removed.
- Write a business case for investing in product telemetry.

Limitations: the lifecycle skills read and write files in the user's repository, so this plugin is available in Codex only. The skills generate plans and code only; they do not send any data to Accoil or to analytics vendors, do not create analytics accounts, and do not define KPIs or build dashboards. Review generated code before merging.

release.description: Guides you through finding the reasoning events that change a language model's outcome with the open-source PTS framework.

interface.short_description: Find pivotal reasoning events
interface.long_description: Guides you through PTS (Pivotal Token Search), an open-source framework for finding the reasoning events that change whether a language model solves a task. The workflow explains the three scales PTS searches (latent workspace meta-tokens, emitted pivotal tokens, and reasoning sentences called thought anchors), installs PTS from its README after asking you, and shows how to run a search on a task with a small local model. It explains how to read the output: probability shifts, the shared category labels, and why latent readout scores are not comparable to probability changes. It covers the hosted visualizer, linking events into chains, and exporting results as datasets for preference tuning or steering. It states the limits plainly: searches are expensive because they sample many continuations, results are observational unless you run an intervention with controls, and findings depend on the task, the model and the sampling settings. This plugin contains instructions only; everything runs on your own machine.

release.description: Track your net worth across cash, investments, crypto, property and debts, keep balances and statements up to date, and review spending from banks connected in Wealth Tracker.

interface.short_description: Your net worth and spending
interface.long_description:
Wealth Tracker keeps your whole net worth in one place: cash and savings, investments, crypto, property, vehicles and other valuables, minus mortgages, loans and other debts. Connect it to ChatGPT to ask about your money in plain words and keep your records up to date from the conversation.

What you can do:
- See your net worth, totals, allocation and liquidity, how they have moved over time, and the income your holdings earned.
- Find any holding by name, ticker or ISIN, and list everything that is due or out of date for an update.
- Record a balance, a buy or sell you have already made, interest or a fee, or a whole account statement or screenshot at once. Every change can be previewed first, returns a receipt, and can be undone within 30 days.
- Choose how often Wealth Tracker reminds you to update an account or a holding.
- If you have connected a bank in the Wealth Tracker app: see spending and income by category, merchant and period, search your transactions, review subscriptions and other recurring payments, recategorise transactions, and mark a recurring payment as confirmed, dismissed or cancelled in your records.

What it does not do:
- It never moves money, makes payments or places trades. Buys and sells are records of trades you made elsewhere.
- Bank data is read-only. It cannot connect a bank, sign in to your bank or broker, or change anything at your bank or at a merchant. Bank connections are set up in the Wealth Tracker app.
- It reads and changes only the signed-in user's own Wealth Tracker records, and sees nothing you have not added to Wealth Tracker.
- It reports your own figures and does not give investment, tax or financial advice.

You need a Wealth Tracker account and sign in with it when you connect.
capabilities: Read net worth, allocation and holdings
Read net worth history and income earned
List holdings that need an update
Record balances, trades, income and fees
Sync an account statement or screenshot
Read spending, transactions and subscriptions from connected banks

- AI Unicode Remover (strips invisible characters from AI-generated text)

Tests that need the full browser (webcam, dead pixel, CPU/GPU stress test, favicon checker/generator, tag checker, song key finder) open on helptester.com.

interface.long_description:
Zone2AI estimates your Zone 2 heart rate range, the easy aerobic intensity that builds endurance, using the same method as the Zone2AI app. Give your age, and your resting heart rate if you know it; a max heart rate you have actually measured makes it more precise. You get the range in beats per minute, a plain line on how it was estimated, and the talk test to check it in your next session. It works for running, cycling and walking, for people aged 16 to 90 who train for general fitness. No sign-in is needed.

If you mention a heart condition, chest pain, heart-rate medication or pregnancy, ChatGPT tells Zone2AI only that, so it can decline to give a range; nothing is stored. In those cases Zone2AI gives no range and suggests asking your clinician instead.

Limitations: the range is an estimate for general fitness, not medical advice. Zone2AI covers Zone 2 only, not other heart-rate zones, workout plans or medical questions. The result card includes a link to the Zone2AI app and one to its website.
capabilities: Estimate your Zone 2 heart rate range

release.description: Website monitoring your AI assistant can run: add sites, set up and run monitors, read health, performance and uptime, review results with undo, and apply the fix a run proposes.

interface.short_description: Monitor and fix your websites
interface.long_description:
Relvato monitors websites in a real browser: sign-ups, logins, checkout, payments, page speed, search visibility and security. It runs its monitors on a schedule and again every time the site changes, and it works on any website, going deepest on WordPress and WooCommerce.

This plugin brings your Relvato account into ChatGPT. Sign in once, then ask in plain words:
- "Which of my sites needs attention right now?"
- "Why did checkout fail last night, and how do I fix it?"
- "How fast is my shop for real visitors, and what slows it down?"
- "Add my product pages to the visual monitor and run it."

What ChatGPT can do with it:
- Set up: add a site, walk you through proving it's yours (the WordPress plugin or a DNS record), and pick monitors for your goals.
- Configure: schedules, re-runs after WordPress updates, the pages the visual monitor compares, checkout details, and custom monitors Relvato's AI writes from a plain-language goal.
- Read: health and uptime, real-visitor and lab Core Web Vitals, each run's findings with screenshots, WordPress updates and the activity log.
- Act: run monitors now, get the brief for fixing a failure, and on WordPress apply the one fix a run proposes or update a vulnerable plugin, with automatic undo if anything breaks.
- Review: when you confirm a change is intended, accept a new screenshot or page structure, or ignore a finding. Every such decision can be undone.

You stay in control. Tools that change your site are marked so ChatGPT asks you first. ChatGPT works within your Relvato account's limits, can't skip proving a site is yours, and can't approve file-integrity, script or DNS changes, change who receives your alerts, see secrets, delete data or touch billing. Those stay in the Relvato dashboard.

Sign-in uses your Relvato account, and you can disconnect ChatGPT at any time under MCP connector → Connected assistants.

release.description: Check whether AI assistants and AI search engines can fetch, read and cite a public website, with a score and specific fixes.

interface.short_description: Can AI read and cite your site
interface.long_description:
AIOScan checks whether AI assistants and AI search engines can fetch, read and cite a public website.

Give it a website or domain and it returns a 0 to 100 AI visibility score, the checks that failed, and the specific fix for each one, with a link to the full report. Typical findings: AI crawlers blocked in robots.txt or by a firewall, key content that only appears after JavaScript runs, missing structured data, and unclear page titles and headings.

What it does not do: it does not tell you whether AI currently names your business in answers, and it cannot guarantee any ranking or citation.

How it works: AIOScan fetches the page the way a normal visitor would and again the way an AI crawler would, then runs 21 published checks on the results. It scans one public address per request, only reads public pages, and never logs in to anything. Only the address you provide is sent to AIOScan. No account needed.
capabilities: Scan a website for AI visibility

It covers saving and loading and states the limits plainly, including order dependence in online learning and the cost of wrong pooling or blend settings. This plugin contains instructions only; everything runs on your own machine.

release.description: Everythings is a workspace app for notes, lists, and the work your AI agents produce. This plugin lets ChatGPT and Codex search, read and write things in your workspaces, ask you a question on a thing, and read your answer on the next run.

interface.short_description: Review what your agents write
interface.long_description:
Everythings is a workspace app for notes, lists, and the work your AI agents produce. It is made for people who run coding agents across several projects and want to read, approve, and correct what those agents write from wherever they are, including a phone.

A workspace holds a tree of "things". A thing is one unit of work: a name, a Markdown body, and a position among other things. Things nest, so a plan sits under its project and a decision sits under its plan. Marks are emoji reactions on a thing, and comments are threaded discussion on it.

This plugin lets ChatGPT and Codex read and write that structure directly.

What the plugin can do:

- Search every workspace you have access to, by name, tags, or body text
- Read a thing's full content, along with its sub-things, comments, and marks
- Create and edit things, nest them, reorder them, and move or copy them between workspaces
- Create and rename workspaces
- Add comments and react with emoji marks
- Ask you a question on a thing, and read your answer later
- Show a workspace or a thing as the Everythings view inside the chat, where ChatGPT renders app views

How the review loop works:

An agent working on a task creates a thing for each result: a plan, a set of findings, a log entry from a scheduled run. When it needs a decision, it attaches a question to the thing, with options if it has them, and stops. The question waits on the thing, appears in your inbox, and Everythings can notify you. You answer from your phone or the web, or tell the agent in the chat, and the agent reads the answer on its next run. Every thing, comment, and mark an agent writes carries the agent's name, so its work is easy to tell from yours. Comments tell the agent what to change. Marks are your own record of what you reviewed, and the agent can read them back. A new workspace can start from the Agent workflow template, which lays out Agent tasks, Human tasks, Plans, and Logs.

For everyday use, ask it to keep what you just worked out ("save this under Travel") or to bring back something from months ago ("what did we decide about the roof?").

Read tools are annotated read-only, so they run without a confirmation each time. Editing a thing, deleting one, renaming a workspace, and removing a mark are annotated destructive, so ChatGPT confirms them with you first. interface.short_description: Senior Google Ads advice
interface.long_description:
Answers to Google Ads questions the way a senior paid search manager gives them: the verdict first, the numbers that decide it, the next action, and what would change the answer. No generic checklists.

- No BS PPC: bidding, budgets, keywords, match types, negatives, Performance Max, AI Max, Demand Gen, ad copy and tracking. Corrects common mistakes (Ad Strength as a KPI, bid adjustments under Smart Bidding, scaling brand, reading immature conversions) with the reason and the number.
- Performance triage: from a campaign report with a date segment, splits a change in CPA or conversions into demand, impression share, CTR, CPC and conversion rate, by segment (brand, non-brand, PMax, app, upper funnel), and separates mix shift from real change.
- Search terms cleanup: n-gram analysis of a search terms report, negative keyword candidates that do not block converting traffic, and routing decisions for competitor, geo and brand terms.
- Account quick audit: measurement, bidding, structure, queries, ads and efficiency in order of money at stake, with evidence for each finding.
- RSA review: writes and checks responsive search ads against character limits and the editorial rules that cause disapprovals.
- Bid targets: target CPA or ROAS from margin, lifetime value and funnel rates, not from last quarter's results.
- Budget pacing: month-to-date spend, forecast and the daily spend needed to land on budget.
- Auction insights: who gained share, who is new, who ranks above you.
- Change history review: target changes inside the calibration window, large swings, auto-applied recommendations, and which change lines up with a performance shift.

Platform facts (limits, dates, policies) are checked against Google's help pages and cited. Report exports in English and Spanish are read directly, including the interface's preamble and totals rows.

release.description:

release.description: Capable Cap Table in ChatGPT: fully diluted ownership, stock options and vesting, SAFEs and convertible notes, 409A valuations, round dilution and exit waterfalls, with changes drafted for an admin to approve.

interface.short_description: AI-native cap table platform
interface.long_description:
Capable Cap Table connects ChatGPT to your startup's cap table in Capable, the AI-native cap table and equity management platform. Ask about ownership, equity and fundraising in plain language, and draft changes for an admin to approve.

Founders, finance, legal and HR admins can:
- See who owns what on a fully diluted basis, by stakeholder and by share class, including the option pool.
- Look up any stakeholder's stock options (ISO and NSO), RSUs, restricted stock (RSAs), warrants, SAFEs and convertible notes.
- Check vesting schedules, cliffs and the next vesting dates.
- Check the current 409A valuation, its fair market value per share and when it expires.
- Model a priced round (Seed, Series A and later), including SAFE and note conversion and an option pool top-up, and see the dilution for each holder.
- Model an exit and see what each holder takes home after liquidation preferences.
- Get links to export the cap table to Excel, CSV or OCF, and review recent activity and pending proposals.

Employees, advisors and investors can ask about their own equity: how much has vested, the next vesting dates, exercise prices and deadlines.

Example questions:
- Who owns what in our cap table, fully diluted?
- List our outstanding SAFEs with their valuation caps.
- How much will the founders be diluted if we raise $10M at a $40M pre-money valuation?
- When does our 409A expire?
- If we sell the company for $150M, what does each holder take home?

ChatGPT can draft a change, such as a new stakeholder, an option grant, a termination, a cancellation or a 409A record, as a proposal. Nothing changes until an admin approves the proposal inside Capable.

Capable shows each person only what they are allowed to see. Round and exit models are planning estimates, not tax, legal or investment advice. The plugin does not move money or place trades.

interface.long_description: FIONA is a writing and productivity assistant for non-clinical beauty businesses, such as hair salons, barbers, manicure businesses and makeup professionals. Its main purpose is to draft customer-service messages about known prices, service descriptions, opening hours, available appointment slots, payment terms, cancellations and commercial questions. Users provide anonymized messages and confirmed business facts. FIONA uses the FIO Method—Fact, Intention and Guidance—to interpret the conversation, draft up to three useful reply options and refine the chosen text. Professora mode teaches reusable message shortcuts, labels, catalogs and administrative WhatsApp Business routines. The package contains curated commercial communication references only. It does not support healthcare services, clinical aesthetic procedures, health-information workflows, provider matching, diagnosis, treatment recommendations or clinical aftercare. It does not send WhatsApp messages, access calendars, book appointments, process payments or store its own customer database. Users review all drafts before sending; no sales outcome is guaranteed.

release.description: Search Arca's public life-sciences corpus: FDA drug and device records, clinical trials, PubMed literature, VAERS, CDC data, and EU/PMDA device vigilance.

interface.short_description: Search FDA, trials and PubMed
interface.long_description:
Arca Life Sciences searches a curated index of public regulatory, clinical, and scientific records and returns results with links to the original source.

What you can search:
- FDA drug records: labels, Drugs@FDA approvals and review documents, complete response letters, warning letters, Form 483s, inspections, import refusals, Orange Book, Purple Book, NDC, drug shortages, and postmarket requirements
- FDA device records: 510(k), PMA, registrations, GUDID, and MAUDE adverse event reports
- ClinicalTrials.gov studies
- PubMed and Europe PMC literature, ranked with citation counts and open-access status
- VAERS, CDC public-health data, EU expert panels, and BfArM/PMDA device vigilance

Who it is for: regulatory affairs, quality, pharmacovigilance, clinical, and medical-affairs teams, and anyone researching drugs, devices, or the evidence behind them.

Limitations: it only searches public records that Arca mirrors, so it has no access to your own documents, patient data, or non-public FDA correspondence. It is read-only and cannot file reports or submissions. Results are research material, not medical advice.

release.description: Work with your company's books in Vezna: cash, P&L, spending, the VAT estimate and the general ledger, plus the invoices and answers Vezna is still waiting for.

interface.short_description: Your company's books, in chat
interface.long_description:
Vezna is an AI-native accounting firm for Bulgarian companies. Its agents keep the books from your bank feeds and invoices, matching every payment to its document and asking when something is missing, and accountants review the work and file the returns.

Connect Vezna to ChatGPT to work with your company's books in plain language:

• Ask about cash across your accounts, monthly P&L, spending by category, revenue by client, and the estimated VAT position with its filing deadline.
• Look into the general ledger: the trial balance, accrual P&L, who owes whom, the draft VAT return, and why each journal entry was proposed.
• See what Vezna is still waiting on this month (payments without an invoice, invoices to issue, unexplained bank lines) and close the gaps: search the company mailbox for a missing invoice, submit it to Vezna, or answer Vezna's question about a payment.

Figures come from Vezna's own calculations over your books. VAT figures are estimates and ledger figures are drafts until your accountant reviews them; your accountant files the returns.

Vezna can't make payments, file returns, approve ledger entries, change settings or delete data. Personal identification numbers (ЕГН/ЛНЧ) and full card numbers are masked in every result, and every tool call is logged in Vezna, where you can revoke the connection at any time.

Requires a Vezna account as an owner or team member of the company. Searching and filing from email also needs the company's Gmail mailbox to be connected to Vezna.

interface.short_description: Personalized PDFs from a sheet
interface.long_description:
Mail merge from Excel or CSV to PDF, right in the chat. Attach a spreadsheet or paste a list, write the letter once with fields like {{First Name}}, and get one print-ready PDF with a personalized document for each row.

What it makes:
- Mail merge letters: personalized letters from your spreadsheet in US business letter layout, with your return address, the date, the recipient's address, an optional subject line, a closing and a signature (thank-you letters to donors, the same letter to 200 customers with their names)
- Certificates in bulk from a name list: award, completion, participation and appreciation certificates on landscape US Letter, in 4 styles (classic, gold, modern, deco) with signature lines
- Envelopes from a contact list: #10 business envelopes (or A7) with your return address and the delivery address placed inside the USPS read area, optionally in USPS uppercase style

It checks the merge before printing:
- Template fields with no matching column, with the closest column name
- Similar column names matched for you (first_name for First Name, Zip Code for ZIP) and reported, so you can confirm them
- Records with empty values, listed by record number before you generate
- ZIP codes that lost a leading zero in Excel (2134 becomes 02134)

Template features: defaults {{First Name|Friend}}, formats {{Amount:currency}}, {{Gift Date:date}}, {{Place:ordinal}}, and conditions {{#if Company}}...{{else}}...{{/if}}. You see the first 3 merged records and can step through each record in the preview. Each PDF holds up to 2,000 records, and a merge report CSV lists the values printed for each record.

Limitations: it makes PDFs only. It does not send email, connect to Word, Outlook or Gmail, or print and mail anything, and it does not make mailing labels, diplomas, degrees or licenses. Latin with accents (for example Polish or Vietnamese), Greek and Cyrillic print as typed; Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew and emoji cannot be printed. interface.short_description: Hosted multilingual websites
interface.long_description:
Create, edit, and host multilingual websites directly through chatting with ChatGPT. Ask ChatGPT to create your pages in your native language, and Croisa can translate them into the languages on your site, with localized URLs and language routing.

A visitor who cannot read your site does not become a customer. If you run a restaurant, a salon, a contractor, or any local business where people speak more than one language, a menu, a price list, your hours, and your address in only your language sends everyone else to a competitor they can understand.

The next change is the expensive part. A new dish, a new service, a holiday schedule, or a new price makes the other language wrong unless you rewrite it, hire a translator, or keep a second site. You write it once, in the language you already use with ChatGPT. Croisa can update your other site languages from that change.

Most owners do not have a web person anymore. The site was built once and the login is gone, or there is no site at all, only photos and a phone number. You should not have to learn a builder or start a website project. Describe the business in the chat. Croisa creates the pages and hosts them.

If you already have a site and it is stuck in one language, bring it to Croisa. Make it bilingual, put it on your own domain, and let people contact you in the language they actually read. When someone looks you up in their language, each language has its own URL, and they land on the one that matches them.

release.description: Research Turkish public and private law through legislation, article texts and legislative rationales, public court decisions and GİB private tax rulings, with source links and citations.

interface.short_description: Turkish law & source analysis
interface.long_description:
Mütalaa supports Turkish legal research across public and private law through legislation, legislative rationales, public court decisions and Turkish Revenue Administration (GİB) private tax rulings. Find and read primary sources, examine legal concepts and institutions, and compare provisions, judicial reasoning and administrative interpretations with source links and citations.

Use it to study a legal subject, map the rules governing an activity or relationship, examine how a provision is interpreted and applied, or investigate a specific document. It supports professional and academic research, legal education, and source research for legal opinions, pleadings, contracts, regulatory compliance assessments and organizational decisions. Research can address substantive and procedural rules, requirements and exceptions, powers and jurisdiction, rights and obligations, liability, sanctions and remedies.

Research spans civil and commercial law, companies, enforcement and insolvency, employment and social security, consumer protection, property, family and inheritance, criminal law, public administration, taxation, constitutional law and other Turkish legal subjects represented in the available sources.

Search legislation by topic, title, number or Official Gazette details. Sources include laws, decree-laws, presidential decrees, regulations, communiqués and available repealed instruments. Read full texts or specific articles, inspect chapter and article structures, search within legislation, and retrieve general or article-level legislative rationales where available. Distinguish legislative rationales from enacted provisions.

Find public court decisions by legal issue and, where supported, court or chamber, date, and case or decision number. Sources include Yargıtay civil and criminal chambers, Danıştay, regional appellate civil courts, first-instance civil courts, the kanun yararına bozma collection and Constitutional Court (AYM) constitutional review and individual applications. Read and compare the facts, reasoning and outcomes of decisions alongside the relevant legislation. Research GİB private rulings as administrative tax interpretations tied to their facts and period.

Connect a Mütalaa account and keep research inputs anonymous. Mütalaa provides legal information and source research; legal representation, submitting applications and access to private UYAP files are outside its scope. Foreign-law-only research and searches of regional criminal appellate or regional administrative courts are outside this release. Coverage depends on the available sources; exhaustive coverage, historical versions and instant updates are not guaranteed.
capabilities: Find and compare Turkish court decisions

InfoGrunt może pokazać m.in.:

identyfikację i geometrię działki,
dane ewidencyjne,

dostęp i kontekst drogowy,

publiczne dane cenowe dla gminy oraz informacje o zmianach na rynku.

Performance Coach turns ChatGPT into a communication coach built on RapportScore's open coach brain, the same science-based, AI-enhanced craft system that powers coaching inside RapportScore.

What you get:

A real coaching method. Every lesson traces to deterministic conversation measurements: talk time and turns, question structure, interruptions, response latency, backchannels, silence mechanics, and more than two dozen others, each documented in plain language.

The 7 Rapport Dimensions. Active Listening, Curiosity, Emotional Acknowledgment, Engagement, Mirroring, Responsiveness, and Trust Building, with concrete behaviors and drills for each.

Belt progression. A white-to-black belt ladder with clear gates, so practice compounds instead of wandering.

Drills and session types. Debriefs, roleplay reps, pre-call prep, and a drills library with one countable rep per commitment.

Coach on your own calls. Connect your RapportScore account and the coach moves from craft theory to your actual conversations: it fetches your recorded sessions, scores, transcripts, and progress, and coaches with receipts, citing the exact moments in your own calls. Without an account it still teaches the full craft system; it never invents your personal scores.

RapportScore measures behavior, not truth: results describe how a conversation went, never honesty, intent, or who someone is. A RapportScore account is required for personal data.

TerraLab gets map data into QGIS from a conversation. Ask for buildings, roads, addresses, land use, waterways, transit stops or protected areas around any place, see them on an interactive map with a street or aerial view, and download them as Shapefile, GeoJSON, KML or CSV that open directly in QGIS. Limits: extracts up to 20,000 features and 200 km² for buildings (larger for other layers), contour lines up to about 10 x 10 km, files up to 50 MB and lists up to 100 addresses. interface.short_description: Read, compare & audit PDFs
interface.long_description: DocVision AI is a stateless MCP document-intelligence connector for PDFs. From a file you provide (base64 or URL) it opens and inspects the document (pages, geometry, metadata, SHA-256 fingerprint), extracts the real text page by page with x/y provenance, runs OCR on scanned pages, searches, and performs page operations (rotate, delete, extract, reorder, split, merge) that always return a NEW PDF rather than modifying the original. It compares two documents and flags changed amounts, dates and IDs; extracts invoice/form fields where each value is marked SUPPORTED_BY_SOURCE with its provenance and absent values stay UNKNOWN; detects personal data to redact and returns it already masked; and keeps a persistent Document-OS layer (immutable versions, fields, annotations, patches, reviews, batches, RBAC policy, audit). It blocks internal/metadata URLs (anti-SSRF), refuses to empty a document, and does not authenticate signatures or assert a forgery verdict; forensics flags anomalies only.

release.description: Convert bank and credit card statement PDFs to Excel or CSV, reconciled to the cent.
keywords: money in and out by month

interface.short_description: Bank statement to spreadsheet
interface.long_description:
Turn a bank or credit card statement into a spreadsheet of transactions and check that it balances to the cent. Attach a bank or credit card statement (a text PDF from your bank's website, or its CSV or Excel export) and Tallyproof Bank Statements extracts each transaction: date, description, signed amount (money out negative), running balance when printed, and a suggested category.

The key step is reconciliation. It finds the opening and closing balance on the statement and checks opening + money in - money out = closing to the cent. You see PASS, or the difference in dollars and cents and the rows to look at: where the running balance breaks, a likely missing deposit or withdrawal, a duplicated row, or a reversed sign. Deposit and withdrawal totals are compared with the statement's own totals.

It handles real statement layouts: one signed amount column, separate withdrawal and deposit columns, separate deposit and withdrawal sections, CR/DR suffixes, negatives in parentheses, thousands separators, multi-page statements with repeated headers, descriptions that wrap onto a second line, and dates without a year (placed inside the statement period, including December to January). Bank CSV and Excel exports are cleaned into the same format, newest-first or not.

Downloads: an Excel workbook (transactions, reconciliation, totals by month and by category), a clean CSV, and a QuickBooks-ready CSV (Date, Description, Amount). You can also paste or list transactions to reconcile them or total money in and out by month and category.

Good for bookkeepers, freelancers and small businesses doing monthly books or taxes, and anyone preparing statements for a loan application.

Limitations: text PDFs only (scanned or photographed statements need OCR first); up to 60 pages and 20,000 transactions per file. Account numbers are masked to the last 4 digits. Files are read once and downloads expire after about an hour. Categories are keyword suggestions, not accounting or tax advice.

Cats.com Feeding Plan turns a few facts about your cat into a daily feeding plan built from the Cats.com catalogue of cat foods.

What you get:
- A daily calorie target for a healthy adult cat (from one year), computed with the Cats.com formula from weight, age, neuter status and body condition.
- Up to three complete-food plans - wet, dry or a mix - with the exact daily amount of each food (cans, pouches, cups or grams), calories, cost per day and per 30 days in US dollars from a dated price snapshot, the first-order cost, two meals a day and a 7-10-day switch-over schedule. Boundaries: the plan covers healthy adult cats only. Kittens, pregnant or nursing cats, cats with a diagnosed disease, a prescribed diet or current symptoms, and cats with body condition 1 or 5 of 5 get guidance and a referral to their veterinarian instead of a plan; cats with body condition 2 or 4 get a weight-management target with a confirm-with-your-vet note first. Products and prices are from the US market. This is a general guide, not veterinary advice.

When you buy through links, Cats.com may earn a commission; it never affects which foods are chosen. The plugin needs no account and keeps no profile of you or your cat.

- Assemblies with joints that move, such as hinges, arms and linkages. WebCAD reports parts that collide or come apart as a joint moves through its range.
- Gear pairs and simple drivetrains.
- A first stress check of a part: a material, a fixed face and a load, with the peak stress and how far the part bends.

What you get:
- Every build reports PASS, or FAIL with the problems found, so the assistant can fix them before it calls a part done.
- Pictures of the model from the directions you ask for.
- A STEP file, made only when the build passes. Download links work for 24 hours.
- In assistants that show apps in the conversation, a 3D view of the part that you can turn and zoom, with a STEP button.

Limits:
- A PASS means the model builds in WebCAD. Whether a part is right for its purpose (fit, strength, safety, manufacturability) still needs a person's review.
- Stress results are a first check for a person to review, not an engineering sign-off.
- A build takes from about 15 seconds to a few minutes.

release.description: Weekly employee shift schedules that respect availability, roles, max hours, overtime and rest rules, with PDF, Excel and calendar exports.

interface.short_description: Weekly staff shift schedules
interface.long_description:
Rotawise Shift Scheduler makes weekly employee shift schedules for small teams: restaurants, coffee shops, retail stores and clinic front desks. Tell it who is on the team (roles or skills, days and times each person cannot work, minimum and maximum hours) and which shifts you need covered each day (start, end, role and how many people), or attach your availability spreadsheet as CSV or Excel, and it builds the work schedule for the week.

A constraint solver checks each hard rule before it assigns anyone: roles, availability, max hours, the 40-hour overtime line (or overtime allowed only when needed), minimum rest between a closing and an opening shift (the clopening rule, 10 hours by default), shifts per day and days in a row. If a shift cannot be covered, it names the shift and the reason, for example that only two people can work Saturday 6 to 2 as a cook, or that everyone else would go over 40 hours. Weekend and closing shifts are rotated fairly and hours are balanced across the team.

You get hours per person, overtime flags and fairness ranges, a week grid in the chat (by person or by day) where you can take someone off a shift or allow overtime and re-solve, a printable landscape PDF to post, an Excel workbook, and a calendar file (.ics) for each employee. Overnight shifts and daylight-saving weeks are counted in real hours.

Already have a schedule? Check it against your rules: double bookings, clopenings, overtime, too many days in a row, wrong role or a day off that was scheduled.

Limits: one week at a time, up to 80 staff and 400 people-shifts. The rules are the ones you set; it does not know state or city scheduling laws and is not legal advice. It does not publish schedules, message staff, track time or run payroll.

interface.long_description: A practice for working with caveats, drawn from the Caveatist Archive. Mark what kind of statement you are adding (observed, tested, proposed, analogy, mythological, rejected, unresolved); state grounds separately from everything that influenced you; ask what changes if a caveat is true; decide with the unresolved caveats written into the decision; withdraw rather than erase. Each decision or review ends with a fixed record: the decision, its grounds, the caveats it retains, those not pursued, any withdrawals and what would reopen it; the skill includes a worked example. release.description: The real moon phase on any date and the night sky over any city, as printable keepsakes.

interface.short_description: Moon phases & star map posters
interface.long_description:
See the real Moon and the real night sky for the dates that matter: a birthday, a wedding, the night you met.

Moon & Star Map computes the Moon phase for any date from 1800 to 2200 with astronomical algorithms (Jean Meeus): the phase name, the exact illumination percentage, the moon age in days, whether it was waxing or waning, the exact times of the new, quarter and full moons, and the next full and new moon. Give two birthdays and it tells you whether your moons "complete each other" (half a lunar cycle apart, so one moon's light fills the other's shadow), with a match score and an honest explanation. Ask for a month and you get a moon phase calendar with every day drawn.

For a star map, name a city, a date and a local time. Time zones and daylight saving time are handled for you, and the city match is stated in the reply. The map shows about 2,900 stars from the Yale Bright Star Catalog sized by brightness, the constellation lines, the horizon, the cardinal points and the Moon in its real position and phase. You see a live preview, can switch between four styles (midnight, black, paper, ink) and toggle lines and labels, then download vector poster PDFs at 12x18 in, 18x24 in, A3, US Letter and A4 (with 0.125 in print bleed), an SVG, and a share page anyone can open.

Moon posters: one date's moon as a large print, two dates side by side for couples, or a lunar calendar of a whole year.

Good for anniversary, wedding, birthday and new-baby keepsakes, classroom moon charts, and answering "what was the moon on the day I was born?".

Accuracy: moon illumination matches an independent ephemeris within 0.5 percentage points and phase times within about a minute for 1900-2100; star positions match within 0.1 degree.

Limitations: decorative keepsakes, not for navigation or telescope pointing. Planets, the Milky Way and eclipses are not drawn. Cities come from a list of about 11,000 places; give a nearby larger city if yours is missing. PDF text covers Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters; Chinese, Japanese and Korean titles appear in the SVG only.

Data: GeoNames (CC BY 4.0), Yale Bright Star Catalog, constellation lines from d3-celestial by Olaf Frohn (BSD-3-Clause), astronomia (MIT).

release.description: Turn your trips into an IRS-style mileage log and reimbursement total.

interface.short_description: Mileage log and reimbursement
interface.long_description:
Turn your trips into a mileage log for taxes or an expense report, with the reimbursement worked out to the cent. Type your trips ("Oct 5 office to Client A, sales meeting, 12.4 mi"), describe a repeating drive ("weekdays in October, 18 mi to the clinic"), or attach a CSV or Excel file with dates, destinations, purposes and miles or odometer readings.

Each trip gets the IRS standard mileage rate for its date: 70 cents per business mile in 2025, 72.5 cents from January 1 to June 30, 2026, and 76 cents from July 1, 2026 (IRS Notice 2026-10 and Announcement 2026-11). Medical, military moving and charity miles use their own rates. You can also use your employer's rate, for example 60 cents a mile, and see the IRS amount next to it.

What it checks: odometer continuity between trips (overlaps and gaps are flagged), round trips given as one-way miles are doubled, home-to-office commuting is flagged because it is not deductible, and trips without a business purpose or destination are listed so you can fix them before you file or submit.

What you get: totals by month, business purpose and client; business-use percentage from your start-of-year and end-of-year odometer; a printable PDF mileage log with the columns the IRS asks for (date, destination, business purpose, miles, odometer); and an Excel (XLSX) workbook with the trips, a summary and the flags. interface.long_description:
Make a crossword puzzle, a word search, or a sudoku right in the chat, play it there, and print it with an answer key.

Word search maker: easy puzzles run words right and down for young kids, medium adds diagonals, and hard hides words in all eight directions including backwards. Play in the chat: type into the crossword with Check, Reveal word and Reveal all; drag across words in the word search; enter digits and pencil notes in sudoku. Print: every puzzle downloads as a printable PDF worksheet with name and date lines and a separate answer key page, in Letter or A4. Limitations: crossword grids are open layouts with blank space around the words (not symmetric newspaper grids), crossword and word search grids use the letters A-Z only (accents are dropped, so words written only in Cyrillic or Greek cannot be placed), PDF titles and clues print in Latin alphabets including Polish, Czech and German, plus Greek and Cyrillic, but not Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic or Hebrew, and sudoku is the classic 9x9 format.

release.description: Self-employment tax and 2026 quarterly estimated tax planner for 1099 workers, with due-date reminders and a PDF worksheet.
keywords: quarterly estimated tax payments due dates 2026
how much should I pay in quarterly taxes
how much to set aside for taxes as a freelancer

interface.short_description: 1099 tax + quarterly payments
interface.long_description:
A self employment tax calculator and quarterly estimated tax planner for 2026. Tell QuarterWise 1099 Tax Planner your 1099 or freelance income, business expenses, and filing status, and it works through the IRS 2026 Form 1040-ES worksheets: self-employment tax on 92.35% of net profit (12.4% Social Security up to the 184,500 dollar wage base, 2.9% Medicare, and the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax), the deductible half of SE tax, the 20% qualified business income (QBI) deduction, and federal income tax with the 2026 brackets and standard deduction.

It answers questions like "I made 60k on 1099, how much do I owe", "how much should I pay in quarterly taxes", and "how much to set aside for taxes as a freelancer". It handles a W-2 job plus a side gig (wages use up the Social Security wage base and paycheck withholding is subtracted), married couples where one or both spouses are self-employed, business losses, the child tax credit, and the new 2026 senior and charitable deductions.

For quarterly estimated taxes it compares 90% of your 2026 tax with 100% of your 2025 tax (110% if your 2025 AGI was over 150,000 dollars), applies the 1,000 dollar rule, and gives the amount for each due date: Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15, 2026 and Jan 15, 2027. Missed a payment? Add what you have paid and it shows what to pay now and at each remaining date.

The result appears as a card in the chat: a waterfall from income through deductions to tax, and four quarterly payment cards with dates, amounts, and status. Download a calendar file (.ics) with reminders before each due date and a printable PDF worksheet laid out like the IRS worksheet, with a payment record.

Good for freelancers, independent contractors, gig workers (DoorDash, Uber, Instacart, Etsy), consultants, and anyone with 1099-NEC or 1099-K income.

Limitations: estimates for planning only, not tax advice. Federal tax for tax year 2026 only; state income tax is not calculated (it tells you if your state has none). Capital gains rates, AMT, net investment income tax, the earned income credit, penalty amounts, and the annualized installment method are not included. Above the 2026 QBI threshold it applies the phase-in using W-2 wages your business paid, with property basis treated as zero. It does not file returns or make payments.
