release.description: SupershopOS is a retail management system for grocery stores and supermarkets in Bangladesh. It covers point of sale with barcode scanning and price look-up codes, stock tracked by batch and expiry date, suppliers, and VAT-compliant receipts. This app lets a store's owner and staff work with their own live store records in plain language.

interface.short_description: Your store's own numbers
interface.long_description:
SupershopOS is a retail management system for grocery stores and supermarkets in Bangladesh. It covers point of sale with barcode scanning and price look-up codes, stock tracked by batch and expiry date, suppliers, and VAT-compliant receipts. This app lets a store's owner and staff work with their own live store records in plain language.

Ask what came in today, split by cash, bKash, Nagad, card and bank, to see what should be in the till. Ask which products are below their reorder level, with a suggested order quantity, so that everyday staples do not run out. Ask what has been written off as damaged or expired, by reason and by product. Ask which stock has not sold in 90 days and what it is worth at cost. Ask how much is owed to each supplier and how long each balance has been outstanding.

With the owner's permission, the app can also record changes. It can ring up a sale, creating a real invoice with a receipt number that takes the payment and updates stock; the assistant confirms the items and the total with the owner before anything is recorded. Refunds stay in the SupershopOS app, behind a manager PIN. It can void a sale within 24 hours if it was entered by mistake: the stock is returned, the payments are reversed, and any amount charged to the customer's store credit account (khata) is credited back. Voiding is off unless the owner grants it specifically, because it is not part of any standard permission set, and the assistant reads the invoice back and asks for a clear yes every time.

It can also open or close a branch's cash drawer against the cash counted; create an item, or change a price, an aisle location or a reorder level; add a product photo through a single-use upload link, and arrange and remove product photos; receive a batch with its expiry date, or receive one serialized unit by its serial number; log an expense; add a supplier; raise a draft purchase order; and record a customer's payment against what they already owe.

Some actions can send a message, and only to people already in the store's records. A sale that names a customer can send that customer one receipt SMS (off by default). A sale that adds to a customer's store credit sends the owner one Telegram message (on by default, if Telegram is linked) and can send that customer one SMS (off by default). Voiding a sale can send the owner one alert, by Telegram or SMS (off by default). No tool accepts a phone number or message text from the chat.

Some changes are also visible to the public. Creating or changing an item or its photos updates the store's online storefront and marketplace listing. If the owner has connected a Meta commerce catalog (off by default), that product is also included in the next hourly sync to Meta, which shows its price, photo and availability on the store's Facebook or Instagram shop. Ringing up or voiding a sale, and receiving stock or a unit, change the availability those pages show. Recording a customer's payment updates the balance on the customer's shared statement link. No tool accepts a Meta account, a recipient or message text from the chat.

When you add a packaged product, the app can search a shared catalog of grocery and household products, so the new item starts with the correct brand, pack size, barcode and product image. Local and unbranded goods, such as loose rice or homemade items, are usually not in the catalog.

Many items are sold loose by weight or volume, so quantities are shown in each item's own unit rather than as a number of packets.

The app only accesses the single store that the signed-in user belongs to, and it cannot reach any other business's data. Amounts are in Bangladeshi Taka, dates and times follow Bangladesh time, and both Bangla and English are supported.

interface.short_description: Check an AI agent's record
interface.long_description:
BlindOracle Agent Trust answers one question before you work with or hire an AI agent: what is its record?

What it does
- Trust badge: a one-line badge for an agent name or wallet, built from BlindOracle's audit registry and settlement history. An agent BlindOracle has never seen comes back as UNVERIFIED with empty fields; the plugin never invents a score.
- Reputation lookup: completed and failed jobs, disputes and the trust-score trend for the same subject.
- Service list: which BlindOracle services exist and which ones can be used from ChatGPT.

How it works
All tools are read-only. Lookups share a daily limit across all ChatGPT users; when it is reached the tool says so and you can try again the next day. Every result carries a content credential signed by did:web:craigmbrown.com, and the result card shows that the signature is attached. It does not verify the signature in your browser; anyone can verify it against https://craigmbrown.com/.well-known/did.json.

What it does not do
The plugin never asks for wallet keys, seed phrases or payment details and never moves funds. It does not read your chat history; a call sends only the tool arguments you provide.

Who it is for
People and teams choosing agents to delegate work to, marketplace operators vetting counterparties, and developers building agent-to-agent workflows who want an independent record before the first transaction.

Limits
BlindOracle's record covers agents that have transacted with or been audited through BlindOracle. A missing record means "no record here", not "unsafe". Badges expire and are reissued; the expiry date is shown with each badge.

release.description: Plan a 30-minute one-on-one with your employee: goal, two topics, exact questions, what not to do and how to close. No names needed.

interface.short_description: Plan a 1:1 with your employee
interface.long_description:
One-on-One Meeting Prep helps managers prepare a 30-minute one-on-one meeting with an employee.

The goal is to build a solid foundation for your productive employees, so they don't look elsewhere and want to keep working productively for the long term. For example: how to talk to a strong salesperson whose results have dropped so that he wants to keep selling, even harder than before.

Tell it the situation — a new hire in their first weeks, dropped results, someone who wants to grow, a remote employee, an annual review, a conflict, a setback, or your very first one-on-one with this person — how long ago you last talked one-on-one, and what you want to leave the meeting with. No names or personal data are needed.

You get a ready plan: the goal of the meeting, the two topics that fit the situation, how to open (word for word), the questions to ask (word for word), what not to do, how to close with a clear agreement, and practical preparation tips.

The plan is built on a manager's field guide of 12 one-on-one topics by Dmytro Tetervak (TDLife): personality, onboarding, growth, feedback about the manager, achievements, work tasks, performance review, coaching, initiative, conflicts, burnout and remote work. Guidance is available in Russian and Ukrainian and is presented in the language you write in.

The plugin does not interpret psychological test results of other people, does not give medical diagnoses and does not help manipulate or covertly dismiss employees.

release.description: Search live UAE property listings on Listint — units, whole properties and developer projects.

interface.short_description: Find property in the UAE
interface.long_description:
Listint is a UAE real-estate marketplace. The app lets people search live property listings by area, price, size, bedrooms, bathrooms, property type, amenities, views, furnishing, ownership and completion status, and open any result on listint.com.

Three kinds of inventory are searchable: units (individual apartments, villas, townhouses and commercial space, offered both for sale and to rent), properties (whole assets such as residential and mixed-use buildings, villa compounds and land, offered for sale) and projects (developer developments, both off-plan and ready). Results render as an inline carousel of listing cards showing the photo, price, bedrooms, bathrooms, size, location, agency and construction progress, with a map view that plots every result and flies to a listing as the user browses. In fullscreen the app shows the result list, the map and the selected listing side by side.

The app is read-only: it searches published listings and links out to listint.com. It does not create, modify or delete anything, does not take payments, and requires no sign-in. Listing data is served from Listint's own index; map tiles come from Mapbox and listing imagery from Listint's CDN.

Coverage is concentrated in the United Arab Emirates — principally Abu Dhabi and Dubai, with some listings in Ras Al Khaimah — alongside a smaller selection of buildings and projects in Egypt, the United Kingdom, Oman, Morocco, Latvia and Ethiopia. Inventory changes continuously, so the app reports when it has nothing in a requested location rather than offering listings elsewhere as matches. All prices are quoted in AED.

Ethica helps employers track the workplace compliance training, policies and notices their employees must complete, and prove it.

In ChatGPT, Ethica does two things:
- Looks up what employers in a US state, city or Canadian province must provide (training, written policies and employee notices), with who it covers, when it's due, the proof to keep and the official source. No account needed.
- For employers who use Ethica, reads their own compliance records after they sign in: who is overdue, one employee's training record, how far along a requirement is, and links to download records for an inspection or audit.

Built for HR managers, business owners and office managers at small and mid-sized employers.

Limitations: Ethica in ChatGPT is read-only. It never assigns training, sends emails or changes a record; that's done in Ethica. Requirement lookups are general information, not legal advice.

SkyAccess is a private jet empty leg marketplace with 5,000+ live empty leg flights from 900+ FAA Part 135 (and international equivalent) certified charter operators. Empty legs are one-way repositioning flights that operators offer when an aircraft would otherwise fly without passengers.

With SkyAccess in ChatGPT you can:
- Search current empty leg flights by departure and arrival city or airport, travel dates, number of passengers and an optional maximum price.
- Look up one flight by its ID for its route, departure time, aircraft type, available seats, amenities and listed whole-aircraft price.
- Get the link to a flight's public listing page on skyaccess.com.
- Get an indicative price range for a private charter between two locations, by aircraft category.

Nothing is purchased or booked in ChatGPT: a charter request takes no payment and creates no booking, and a listing link creates no booking or hold. No SkyAccess account is needed. release.description: Independently verifiable proof that an exact file existed at a given time.

interface.short_description: Proof your files existed
interface.long_description:
Sellat creates independently verifiable proof that an exact file existed at a given moment. Ask to protect a file and a Sellat panel opens in the conversation: your browser computes the file's SHA-256 fingerprint, and only that fingerprint and the file name reach Sellat. The file never leaves your device. Sellat anchors the fingerprint on the public Polygon blockchain in a Merkle batch and attests it on Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps, so anyone can verify the proof later without trusting Sellat.

You can also add a qualified electronic timestamp from FNMT-RCM (eIDAS, RFC 3161) to a proof. It uses one of the qualified seals available in your Sellat account and is only requested when you ask for it.

From here you can:
- Protect a file, or a SHA-256 fingerprint you already have.
- Check the status of a proof: Polygon anchor, Bitcoin confirmation, qualified seal and certificate link.
- List your proofs.
- See your plan, today's budget and the qualified seals you have left.
- Add the FNMT-RCM qualified timestamp to a proof.

Built for freelancers, creators, small businesses and anyone who needs evidence that a document, photo, contract or design existed in a given state at a given time.

Limits: a proof shows that those exact bytes existed no later than the anchored time; on its own it does not prove authorship or ownership. Proofs are anchored in batches, and each proof tells you when its batch is anchored. Files kept in custody, billing and account settings stay in the Sellat dashboard, out of reach of the plugin. It needs a Sellat account. You choose what it may do on the consent screen, the qualified seal is a separate permission, and you can disconnect it at any time from your Sellat dashboard.

release.description: Check whether a cold email setup is ready to send: live sending-domain audit (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, blocklists, domain age), inbox and domain capacity planning, and a 0-100 outbound readiness score with prioritized fixes.

interface.short_description: Check if cold email is ready
interface.long_description:
Mailinite Outbound Readiness tells you whether your cold email setup is ready to send, and what to fix first.

What it does:
- Audits a sending domain with live DNS lookups: MX records, SPF (including the 10-lookup limit and redirect handling), DKIM at common provider selectors, DMARC policy and reporting, domain blocklists (Spamhaus DBL, SURBL, URIBL), domain age from the registry's RDAP record, and whether the domain resolves. Each check returns pass, warn or fail with a specific fix, plus a 0-100 score.
- Plans sending infrastructure for a monthly volume: daily sends, active and spare inboxes, number of sending domains, new prospects needed per month, warm-up time and a three-week ramp. All assumptions (emails per inbox per day, inboxes per domain, spare capacity, warm-up days) can be changed, and you can add your own prices for a cost estimate.
- Scores overall outbound readiness from 0 to 100 by combining the domain audit and capacity plan with your answers about separate sending domains, warm-up, list verification, bounce rate, opt-out, open tracking and ICP, then lists the top fixes in priority order.

Who it's for: founders, sales teams and agencies about to start or scale B2B cold email, and anyone troubleshooting why emails land in spam.

Limitations: it only reads public DNS and registry data and does calculations. It does not send email, change DNS, connect to mailbox or sending accounts, or test actual inbox placement. DKIM keys under custom selectors can't be discovered. Some blocklist operators refuse queries from cloud resolvers, so a list may show as not checked. Results are guidance, not a deliverability guarantee.

No account or sign-in is required, and inputs are not stored.
interface.default_prompt: Is example.com set up correctly for sending cold email?
default_prompts: Is example.com set up correctly for sending cold email?

release.description: Portfolio construction and risk analytics for investment teams: target weights under drawdown, turnover and band constraints, scenario comparison, rebalancing and walk-forward backtests.

interface.short_description: Portfolio construction & risk
interface.long_description:
Allocator Agent brings C8's portfolio-construction engine into ChatGPT. Name the funds you are considering - tickers, ISINs or fund names; their daily history comes from C8's market data - or give it your own return or NAV series, and it computes what the target allocation should be under the constraints you set: per-asset bounds, asset-class bands, a maximum drawdown limit (conditional drawdown at risk, 99%), a turnover cap from your current weights, and a minimum or maximum number of holdings.

What you can do:
- Build a model portfolio with one of fourteen construction methods, from inverse volatility and risk parity to constrained mean-variance and tactical allocation, and see which constraints bind.
- Compare two to five set-ups side by side: what a drawdown cap costs in volatility, what a band changes, what a different method would have held.
- Turn a target into a trade list from your current holdings, within a turnover limit.
- Decompose a portfolio's risk: each holding's contribution, the same by asset class, the gap to your risk budgets, drawdown and concentration.
- Evaluate performance over a period, or run a walk-forward backtest in which the portfolio is rebuilt at each date from the data available on that date only.

Every figure states its source - C8's validated engine, or arithmetic on top of it - and its basis. If a constraint set cannot be met, the answer says so and how close the engine got.

Allocator Agent is decision support for asset managers, wealth managers and investment teams. It works on public price history and the data you provide: it does not give personal investment advice, forecast returns, execute trades or hold client funds. Uploaded series and results are kept for 24 hours so that follow-up questions work, then deleted; holdings quantities and portfolio values are never stored.

No tool changes or deletes your data; results are kept for 24 hours as described above. Requires a C8 Allocator Agent account. You connect with your account email and a one-time code; no API keys.

release.description: Open camera RAW photos in the conversation, read on the user's device and never uploaded, and give them a hand-written look.

interface.short_description: Open RAW photos in chat
interface.long_description:
Rawnd opens camera RAW photos inside the conversation. ChatGPT reads JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF; a NEF, CR3, ARW or RAF file shows it nothing. Rawnd adds a panel where you drop the RAW file. The file is read on your device, inside the panel, and never uploaded: not to Rawnd, not to OpenAI.

What it does
- Shows the JPEG the camera stored inside the RAW file, in under a second, with the shooting data: camera, lens, shutter speed, aperture, ISO and focal length.
- Lets you keep that JPEG (right-click the preview, "Save image as…") or show it to ChatGPT with one click, stripped of its metadata, so you can talk about the photo.
- Offers eight hand-written looks: Dark film, Warm film, High-contrast B&W, Cool & muted, Golden hour, Matte, Crisp & vivid and Teal & orange. ChatGPT picks the one that matches what you describe, can adjust it within narrow bounds ("a bit less warm"), and shows a card that opens it in Rawnd's editor, in the browser.

Who it is for
Photographers with RAW files from Nikon, Canon, Sony, Fujifilm, Panasonic, Olympus, Pentax, Samsung, Leica, Phase One and other cameras, who want to see a RAW file, get a JPEG out of it or pick a look for it, without installing anything. Sixteen formats: CR2, CR3, CRW, NEF, NRW, ARW, SRF, SR2, RAF, DNG, RW2, ORF, PEF, SRW, IIQ and RAW.

Limits
- The panel shows the camera's own rendering, at the size the camera stored: full size on most Nikon and Canon bodies, 1920 × 1280 on Fujifilm. Developing the RAW itself (exposure, white balance) happens in Rawnd's editor.
- Camera RAW files only: it does not open JPEG, PNG or HEIC.
- A look opens in the editor; it is not applied inside the conversation.
- One file at a time.

Privacy
Rawnd's server receives only the tool arguments, a look's name and slider values, and counts one row per call: the tool and the assistant. No account, no sign-in, no photo.

release.description: Explore and estimate roof replacement costs, compare shingle colors and visualize them on your roof, check your roof's storm risk, and look up roof information by address.

interface.short_description: Roof estimator & visualizer
interface.long_description:
GetRoofReport brings roof planning tools into your conversation: a roof visualizer, roof replacement cost calculator, roofing cost estimator, shingle color selector, and address-based roof reports. Explore and estimate roof replacement costs, compare shingle colors and visualize them on your roof, check your roof's storm risk, and look up roof information by address. Plan a new roof, compare colors, review an older roof, or research a house before buying.

ROOF REPLACEMENT COST CALCULATOR AND ESTIMATOR
Ask "How much does a new roof cost?", "What is the roof replacement cost for my house?", or "Open the roofing cost estimator." Use the full interactive roof cost calculator inside the conversation to explore a roof replacement estimate and plan your budget. Enter your address and roof details in the embedded form. The estimator opens without an address-record match. Pricing is calculated inside the estimator; chat details do not automatically fill in its form. Use it when researching the cost to replace a roof or comparing options for a roofing project.

ROOF COLOR VISUALIZER AND SHINGLE COLOR SELECTOR
Ask "What would my roof look like in brown?" or "Show me my house with a different roof color." Upload a house photo inside the roof visualizer to preview shingle colors on your roof. Compare brown, gray, and black shingles and see how a roof color works with your home's siding, brick, trim, and exterior. Use the roofing visualizer to explore roof color ideas before discussing a shingle selection with a contractor.

SHINGLE BRANDS, PRODUCTS, AND COLORS
Browse catalog photos from GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, Atlas, IKO, Malarkey, and TAMKO. Search for GAF Timberline HDZ, Owens Corning Duration, or roof shingle colors such as Charcoal, Weathered Wood, and Driftwood. Ask "Show GAF Timberline HDZ in Charcoal" or "Compare Owens Corning shingle colors." Brand, product-line, and color filters find catalog examples; they do not preselect products in the photo visualizer. Catalog photos are examples, not a rendering of your house.

ROOF AGE AND ROOFING PERMIT LOOKUP
Ask "How old is the roof at this address?" or "Find recorded roofing permits for this house." Resolve an address and review available roof age, roof-age confidence and basis, roofing permits, roof material, shape, and condition score. Reuse the property's report permalink for related lookups. A roof age lookup helps organize recorded information before a roof replacement discussion or home purchase.

STORM RISK ASSESSMENT AND INSURANCE CONTEXT
Ask "What hurricane, hail, and flood exposure is recorded for this property?" Review available hurricane and hail history, FEMA flood-zone information, design wind speed, evacuation zones, and sinkhole proximity. Ask about a records-based roof insurance profile, four-point inspection outlook, inferred wind-mitigation features, or Citizens insurance standing. Historical storm exposure does not establish current roof damage, and records do not guarantee insurance eligibility.

HOME PURCHASE AND ROOF INSPECTION PLANNING
Ask "I'm buying a house. Help me review the roof records, storm risk, and possible replacement needs." Review available records before arranging a roof inspection or discussing the project with a contractor. A virtual review of property records is not an on-site inspection, a diagnosis of current damage, an inspection certificate, or an insurer's coverage decision.

Calculator and visualizer tools can be opened without an address-record lookup. Address-based report availability varies; unsupported addresses may not return records.

release.description: Test your AI agents for security and safety weaknesses, and re-verify the fixes.

interface.short_description: Security testing for AI agents
interface.long_description:
Enoki tests AI agents for security and safety weaknesses. It attacks your agent the way an adversary would, adapts to how the agent responds, and reports each weakness it finds with the exact attack and the agent's response.

With Enoki in ChatGPT you can:
- Register an agent endpoint as a target and keep its profile current.
- Start an assessment, on everything or on the categories a change touched, and follow it to the end.
- Read findings with the full attack transcript, so you can fix the weakness in your code or configuration.
- Close findings, and re-run a finding's attacks against your live agent to confirm a fix worked.

A typical loop: you change your agent's prompt or tools, ask ChatGPT to test the change, read what Enoki found, fix it, and confirm the fix.

You sign in to Enoki and approve the connection, choosing what ChatGPT may do: read only, change targets and findings, or also start assessments. You can change or revoke that at any time under Settings > Connected apps.

Enoki needs an Enoki workspace; an owner or admin of the workspace approves the connection. Register a test or staging deployment of your agent rather than production, because an assessment sends adversarial messages to it.

Find the right New York City school, and the neighborhood around it. Motley NYC answers families' questions from Motley's data on all 262 NYC neighborhoods and on public, charter and private K-12 schools across the five boroughs.

What you can ask:
- Which neighborhoods fit what matters to your family, ranked by your priorities (playgrounds near home can count too) or compared side by side
- How each neighborhood score is computed, and lists of neighborhoods and schools picked by a stated rule

- New York City only.

- At elementary level, in-zone students get a guaranteed seat. Some areas, like all of District 1, have no zoned school.
- We never estimate a family's odds of admission. Seats and applicant counts come from NYC MySchools; the competitiveness band beside them is Motley's own reading, not a DOE rating. Most middle schools, and all charter and private schools, have no published applicant counts.
- Neighborhood scores carry the date they were computed. Admission dates are the city's published dates where it has announced them; otherwise we give the usual window and say so.

New organizers can obtain a registration-form link and complete registration themselves. Check workspace access and open the relevant account settings to complete setup personally. Sensitive account and billing details are entered only in the external cabinet.

Workspace features require an organizer account and depend on its permissions and available services. Assigned-seat booking, payment credentials and other file-upload workflows remain in the cabinet. Access is limited to the connected organization and can be revoked in AI connections.

release.description: Does this retailer take offers, and does it price match? Verified answers, checked by a person.

interface.short_description: Verified retailer price terms
interface.long_description:
The Bidit Registry is a public index of online retailers answering two questions a shopper asks before paying the listed price: will this retailer match a lower price, and on what terms, and can I make it an offer instead of paying the sticker price?

Every price-match answer is checked by a person against the retailer's own published policy, with the policy page linked. Where nothing has been verified the answer is unknown, never a guess. A retailer is reported as taking offers only when it is live on Bidit, the negotiation engine for online stores.

Four read-only tools: will_price_match (yes, no or unknown, with terms, exclusions and how to claim), price_policy (everything verified about a retailer's handling of price), retailers_that_price_match (verified retailers in a country and category), and can_make_offer (yes or not yet, with the offer link). No login is needed. The data is open under CC BY 4.0.

Limitations: the Registry reports published policy; it does not negotiate, buy, or check live prices. Coverage is deepest for Australian retailers.

release.description: Turn scripts into ready-to-use voiceover MP3s in ChatGPT: pick from 500+ AI voices, design a new voice from a description, and save voices to your Lazybird library.

interface.short_description: Turn scripts into voiceovers
interface.long_description:
Turn scripts into ready-to-use voiceover MP3s without leaving ChatGPT. Write or polish your script with ChatGPT, then ask Lazybird to read it aloud: you get an audio player in the chat and an MP3 you can download and drop into your video, podcast, ad, audiobook or course.

What you can do:
- Find the right voice by describing it ("a calm British narrator for a nature documentary"). Lazybird searches 500+ voices in 150+ languages and accents, plus the voices in your own library, including your cloned voices.
- Generate speech from any text with the voice you picked, adjusting the speaking speed or the language and accent.
- Design a brand-new voice from a description ("a raspy, ancient wizard with a slow, mysterious delivery"), listen to the sample, and save it to your Lazybird library to reuse in ChatGPT or in Lazybird Studio.
- Check how many characters you have left.

Connect your Lazybird account the first time you use it. Lazybird can't see your password, payment details or API keys, and you can disconnect ChatGPT any time in Lazybird Settings → Connected apps.
capabilities: Search 500+ voices in 150+ languages and accents
Design a new voice from a description
Save voices to your Lazybird library

release.description: Plan your week, check any metric, report on brand deals, schedule posts and answer comments across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and more, right from chat.

interface.short_description: Social media from the chat
interface.long_description:
Zorevo is a social media management platform for creators and small businesses: one place to schedule posts, read analytics, answer comments and DMs, and track brand deals across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads and Bluesky. This plugin lets you do all of that from the chat, with Zorevo cards showing the results.

- Plan my week: finds the open days on your Calendar, uses your own best times and saved notes, and lines up the posts for one approval.
- Analytics: followers, views, likes, comments, shares, saves and engagement for any range, combined or per account, plus monthly recaps.
- Brand deals: add contracts with the signed file, see every post linked to a deal with its numbers, and search your creators and brands.
- Scheduling: schedule, publish or reschedule posts across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky and LinkedIn, or repurpose a post that did well.

interface.short_description: Website launch checks
interface.long_description:
Afterward checks a public website the way a careful launch reviewer would, and tells you what to fix before visitors notice.

Ask in plain language, for example "Check example.com before I launch it." Afterward inspects up to 25 pages of the site, then returns a launch-readiness score with prioritized findings. Each finding shows the evidence Afterward observed and a suggested next step.

What it checks: availability and status codes, HTTPS and redirects, titles and meta descriptions, canonical tags, viewport and Open Graph tags, robots.txt and sitemaps, broken links, image alt text, form security, analytics tags, leftover starter content, and common security headers such as HSTS and Content-Security-Policy.

How it works: Afterward makes read-only requests to public pages, like a browser would. It does not run JavaScript, sign in, or submit forms, and it never contacts private network addresses. It makes no AI calls of its own, so the same site responses always produce the same findings and score. Site owners can opt out with robots.txt.

The score is a launch-readiness indicator only. It is not a security audit, penetration test, compliance check, or accessibility certification.

No account or sign-in is needed. Afterward is made by Entropy Logic.

release.description: Let ChatGPT work on a project on your computer through the Glossa relay and a local worker you start.

interface.short_description: Work on your local project
interface.long_description:
Glossa lets ChatGPT work on a project on your computer. Start Glossa in a project folder and ChatGPT can search and read your code, look at images, make careful edits, and, if you allow it, run your tests, builds, Git, and other commands with the tools you already have installed.

You pick the access for each folder when you start it:
- Read-only: ChatGPT can list, search, and read files and view PNG, JPEG, and WebP images.
- Workspace (the default): ChatGPT can also create, edit, move, and delete files inside that folder. Edits check the file's current version first, so your own changes aren't silently overwritten.
- System: ChatGPT can also run commands. Commands run as your computer account, with its environment, credentials, files, and network access. They aren't sandboxed or limited to the project folder, so turn this on only for an account and machine you're comfortable giving that access.

How it works: the Glossa CLI on your computer connects out to the Glossa relay, so nothing on your machine accepts incoming connections. The relay passes requests to your computer and doesn't store your file contents, command arguments, or command output. Glossa blocks recognizable passwords, API keys, and tokens in file text, edits, and command output before they leave your computer. Images are passed through as they are.

Glossa doesn't add another AI model or agent. ChatGPT does the work, and your plan's usage limits and available features still apply. Don't use Glossa with payment card data, health records, government ID numbers, or account credentials.

To get started, install the CLI with npm install -g @ariobarin/glossa, run glossa in your project folder, and pair your computer when it asks.

release.description: Indicative US 409A and UK EMI share value estimates for private companies, calculated from cap table and financial inputs, plus the documents and process for a formal valuation.

interface.short_description: 409A and EMI value estimates
interface.long_description:
Codon Valuation estimates the value of a private company's common stock (US) or ordinary shares (UK) before a formal valuation.

Give it the company's cap table and finances, such as share counts by class, the last priced round, revenue, cash and debt, and it returns an indicative low, mid and high value per share with the method and every assumption shown. The method follows what the company provides: an option pricing model calibrated to a recent priced round, a roll-forward of an older round blended with a revenue multiple, a sector revenue multiple, or an asset-based range for pre-revenue companies. Value is allocated across share classes with a Black-Scholes option pricing model, then a discount for lack of marketability is applied using the Finnerty and Chaffe models.

It also explains the documents and process for a formal IRC 409A valuation or an HMRC EMI valuation.

All tools are read-only. Nothing is stored, no account is needed, and the tools do not ask for names or other personal information. Results are indicative planning estimates: they are not a 409A valuation, do not provide safe harbor protection, and are not a valuation agreed with HMRC.

Show the valuation method, assumptions and share class allocation behind each estimate
Explain the documents and process for a formal 409A or EMI valuation

interface.long_description:
Ronyxx is an answering service for your business's figures. Your team asks in plain words, and Ronyxx replies with the exact figure, worked out from your company's own records in Odoo ERP: sales and revenue, invoices, what customers owe and which invoices are overdue (accounts receivable), vendor bills and what you owe (accounts payable), cash and bank balances, profit and loss, VAT and tax, quotes and orders, purchases, stock and inventory, deliveries, manufacturing, projects, the CRM pipeline, point of sale, employees and expense claims.

Ask the way you'd ask a colleague: "What were our sales last month?", "Which customers have overdue invoices?", "How many units of the oak desk do we have in stock?". Ronyxx reads the records live and gives the figure with the period it covers. Every figure is calculated by Ronyxx's own tested code from your records; the AI only works out what you're asking. If a question could mean two things, Ronyxx asks which. If it can't answer, it says so rather than guess.

Ronyxx only reads. It can't create, change or delete anything in Odoo. Each person on your team has a role (owner, sales, accounts, purchasing, warehouse, production, HR, or one of your own), and Ronyxx checks it before reading anything, so people see only what their role allows.

To use it, your company needs a Ronyxx account connected to its Odoo (versions 16 to 20), and you need to be on its team with your work email. You sign in with that email and allow the connection.

Ronyxx's answer appears word for word in its own card. Your questions and Ronyxx's answers aren't used to train AI models.

interface.short_description: Your buyer's advocate
interface.long_description:
Judd is your buyer's advocate. Ask Judd before ChatGPT buys, books or reserves something for you, and Judd checks every option against your own preferences. It answers with a clear verdict: YES (go ahead), INSTEAD (choose this better option), FIND_BETTER (search again), NEGOTIATE (ask for a better price or terms), WAIT (the timing is better later), ASK_YOU (you decide), or NO.

Judd works only for you. It is never paid by sellers, takes no commissions, and treats sponsored listings and sales pressure as warning signs, not reasons to buy.

What Judd checks:
- Purchases: the same product from different sellers, the exact model and variant, the all-in price with tax and shipping, return policy, ratings from every review source, and unverified prices.
- Travel: flights, hotels and cars, including refundability, resort fees and taxes charged later.
- Restaurants: time, cost per person, deposits, fees and your dietary and access needs.

Your preferences (budgets, preferred sellers, minimum return windows, protected dates, dining needs such as allergies) live in your Judd account, so every agent you use follows the same rules. Every decision is recorded, and you can see what Judd saved you on your dashboard.

Judd makes recommendations; it never places orders or charges you. Sign in with your Judd key, or get one by email at flowinfo.co/judd.

interface.short_description: Product walkthroughs & guides
interface.long_description:
Layerpath turns screenshots, screen recordings, Loom videos or YouTube links into interactive product walkthroughs with clickable steps and callouts over your real screens. Product, support, sales and training teams use them to explain software workflows. In Layerpath, a walkthrough is called a tour. Sign in with your Layerpath account or create one. Walkthroughs are saved to the workspace you select.

In the chat, you can:
- Create walkthroughs from attached screenshots, screen recordings, Loom videos or YouTube links.
- Find walkthroughs by name, open them and play them in the chat.
- Open a walkthrough in Layerpath's editor to change its steps by hand.
- Edit step text, rename walkthroughs, reorder, merge, hide or delete steps, and change intro and outro content.
- Change callout colors and styles, backgrounds and browser frames.
- Blur private information, including names and email addresses, in screenshots.
- Translate a walkthrough or duplicate it in another language.
- Add voiceover using an AI voice.
- Get share and embed links, or export a walkthrough as a video or a PDF guide.
- Undo a change made through the chat.

When Layerpath creates a walkthrough, it publishes it at a share link accessible to anyone with the link. Requesting a share link, or turning on Publish in Share, also publishes an unpublished walkthrough. Changes to published walkthroughs appear at their share links immediately. You can unpublish or delete walkthroughs in Layerpath. Repeating a creation, duplication or video export request creates another output each time.

Layerpath works with existing screens and walkthroughs in your connected workspace. It doesn't design new interfaces or create text-only documents.

release.description: Solve math problems, calculate statistics and probabilities, graph results, and save reproducible worked explanations.

interface.short_description: Math Solver & Statistics help
interface.long_description:
Julius is a math solver and statistics calculator for equations, calculus, probability, and statistical tests. Solve mathematical problems with Python, inspect the calculation, plot the result, and save an explanation you can review.

Use Julius for:

- Math and algebra: Simplify expressions, factor polynomials, solve equations and systems of equations, work with fractions and logarithms, and check roots against the original problem.

- Calculus Solver: Calculate derivatives, integrals, limits, and series. Work through definite integrals, partial derivatives, and supported differential equations using symbolic or numerical methods.

- Statistics Solver: Find the mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, percentiles, and z-scores. Distinguish sample and population calculations and explore distributions with histograms and boxplots.

- Hypothesis tests: Run t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square tests, and supported nonparametric tests. Calculate p-values, confidence intervals, and effect sizes; explain assumptions and what the results support.

- Probability: Calculate conditional probabilities, expected values, combinations, permutations, and normal, binomial, or Poisson probabilities. Use simulation to explore random variables and uncertainty.

- Linear algebra and graphs: Work with matrices, determinants, inverses, eigenvalues, and vectors. Plot functions, compare equations, and visualize correlations or fitted regression models.

- GCF Calculator: Easily find the greatest common factor for any number seconds. Get tutoring and step-by-step explanations to improve your Math capabilities.

Enter a problem in chat or use observations and source files saved in your personal Julius library. The Julius Math Solver can run Python with appropriate numerical and symbolic packages, generate charts, and save calculations with the method, inputs, assumptions, and results. interface.short_description: Branded QR codes for agents
interface.long_description:
QRsome makes QR codes from the chat and hosts them as SVG for print and PNG for screens.

Ask for a code for a website, a Wi-Fi network, a contact card, an email, a phone number, a text message, a WhatsApp chat, a map location, a calendar event or a social profile, one at a time or in batches within your account allowances (for example one per table, with a ZIP of all of them). Each code appears in an in-chat preview where you can change its shape, color and look, and download it.

Dynamic codes point to a short qrsome.com link: you can change where they go after printing, and see how many times they were scanned, per day, country and referrer. Static codes hold their content directly and never expire.

Save up to 5 brand looks with your shape, color and logo; the logo is taken from your website, a link to the image, or an image you attach in the chat. New codes use your look.

Who it is for: anyone who prints or shares QR codes, such as restaurants, shops, event organizers, marketers and small businesses.

Limitations: each account can keep 10 active dynamic codes and create 100 static codes per calendar month (UTC). Batches count each successful code against these allowances. QRsome makes QR codes only, not barcodes. It needs a QRsome account (sign in with your email when you connect). Only codes made with your account are visible to you. Scan counts are available for dynamic codes only.

skills.name: clause-comparator
skills.description: Compares the same clause or provision across draft rounds, precedents, public agreements or a portfolio and reports what differs in wording and effect. Use for version-change requests and external clause benchmarking, including "what changed between drafts", "compare their indemnity with ours", "compare liability caps across these SaaS agreements", "what indemnity approach is most common in public SaaS agreements", "what is typical", "what is prevalent" or "is this market standard". External frequency claims require a disclosed multi-document sample, not one precedent. Distinct from contract-reviewer, which grades an agreement for risk; this stays neutral unless a side is given. Fires for any clause type in any commercial agreement.

skills.name: contract-drafter

Use for "draft a services agreement", "turn this term sheet into a contract", "prepare an NDA", "draft an SPA from our template", or requests to draft using public agreements, model forms or market examples. When external precedents are requested, it searches the plugin's listed contract sources before generic websites. Distinct from contract-reviewer, which analyses an existing agreement. Fires for any commercial agreement type.

interface.short_description: Draft agreements from a term sheet or instructions
interface.default_prompt: Use $contract-drafter to draft an agreement from this term sheet, in the specified drafting posture.

skills.name: contract-reviewer
skills.description: Reviews an entire draft or executed commercial contract, or an expressly scoped set of related provisions, from one identified party's perspective and produces ranked risks, exact clause citations and negotiation recommendations. Use for prompts such as "review this MSA from the Buyer's side", "what should we push back on across this agreement", "review only the IP and confidentiality provisions", or "conduct an exhaustive audit". Quick review is the default; focused and full-audit modes follow the user's scope. Do not use for a neutral summary, obligation extraction, version comparison, a single-clause rewrite, a focused liability or exit outcome question, or negotiation strategy.

interface.short_description: Rank contract risks from one identified party's side
interface.default_prompt: Use $contract-reviewer to review this agreement from the Buyer's side and rank the 10 most important legal and commercial risks.

skills.name: contract-summariser
skills.description: Produces a short, factual, neutral summary of what a contract actually does — the parties, what is being exchanged, the key commercial terms, and the handful of provisions worth knowing before reading the whole document. Use this when a user wants the gist rather than a review — including phrasings like "what does this contract actually say", "summarise this NDA for me", "give me the two-minute version of this agreement", "what are we actually signing up to", "plain-English rundown of this lease", or "brief the team on what this MSA covers". Neutral by default — it does not take a side or grade risk; hand off to contract-reviewer for that, or to obligations-extractor for a complete deadline ledger. Fires for any commercial agreement type.

skills.name: indemnity-liability-analyst
skills.description: Analyses the warranty, indemnity, exclusion, cap and insurance provisions in a contract as one interacting system for one identified party. Use for focused prompts such as "what is our exposure under this indemnity", "does the cap still protect the Supplier after the carve-outs", "which liabilities are capped or uncapped", or "does the IP indemnity sit inside the cap". Reports stated and functional caps, sub-caps, quantifiable exposure, apparently uncapped categories and unquantifiable dependencies. It does not infer insurance coverage without the actual policy. Distinct from contract-reviewer, which ranks issues across an agreement.

This is a quantification tool, not a merits assessment — it does not decide whether the underlying claim succeeds; pair it with deficiency-analyst or product-liability-analyst for that. Fires for any compensation or damages claim, consumer or otherwise, wherever loss needs to be built up head by head from supplied figures.

interface.short_description: Build a compensation claim head by head

skills.name: consumer-complaint-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a consumer complaint — the formal filing that states the parties, establishes the forum's jurisdiction, particularises the defect, deficiency, or unfair trade practice alleged, and states the relief sought. Use this whenever a user wants to file a consumer complaint — including phrasings like "draft a consumer complaint over this defective appliance", "file a complaint for deficiency in service against this repair shop", "prepare a complaint for the district consumer forum", or "draft the complaint and state what relief we want". Side-specific — drafted for the complainant, against the opposite party. Pairs with compensation-quantifier for the relief figures and deficiency-analyst for a fuller merits test; this skill states the allegation as instructed, it does not independently establish it. Fires for any consumer complaint over goods, services, or an unfair trade practice, in any jurisdiction with a consumer-forum or equivalent process.

interface.default_prompt: Use $consumer-complaint-drafter to draft a consumer complaint on these facts, with jurisdiction, the deficiency alleged, and relief sought.

skills.name: deficiency-analyst
skills.description: Tests whether given facts actually satisfy the legal threshold for deficiency in service, defect in goods, or unfair trade practice, working element by element rather than asserting a conclusion. Use this whenever a user wants to know if a set of facts clears that threshold — including phrasings like "does this actually count as deficiency in service", "is this an unfair trade practice or just a bad experience", "test whether we have a viable consumer complaint here", "what's our exposure if a customer alleges deficiency", or "walk through whether these facts meet the test". Can run for either side — testing whether a consumer has a claim, or whether an opposite party has exposure — ask which. Distinct from consumer-complaint-drafter, which states the allegation as instructed; this tests whether it actually holds up. Fires wherever the deficiency, defect, or unfair-trade-practice threshold is the question, in any jurisdiction with a consumer protection regime.

skills.name: opposite-party-reply-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a reply or written statement to a consumer complaint on behalf of the opposite party — raising any threshold objection prominently, then addressing each allegation as admitted, denied with the client's own account, denied for insufficient knowledge, or qualified. Use this whenever a user has been served a consumer complaint and needs to respond — including phrasings like "draft our reply to this consumer complaint", "prepare a written statement denying these allegations", "we've been named as opposite party, help us respond", "raise a jurisdiction objection and reply on the merits", or "draft our defence before the deadline in this complaint". Side-specific — drafted for the respondent, against the complainant. The consumer-forum counterpart to notice-reply-drafter. Fires for any reply to a consumer complaint, in any jurisdiction with a consumer-forum or equivalent process.
