release.description: Comparative analysis, forum/jurisdiction analysis, issue-spotting, legislative history, precedent mapping, research synthesis, and statutory interpretation skills.

interface.short_description: Legal research workflows
interface.long_description: Seven reusable legal research workflows covering comparative jurisdiction analysis, forum selection, issue-spotting, legislative history, precedent mapping, research synthesis, and statutory interpretation — all built around sourcing discipline rather than asserting legal facts from memory.
interface.default_prompt: Spot every issue and threshold problem in this fact pattern.
default_prompts: Spot every issue and threshold problem in this fact pattern.
Map the authorities on this specific point.
Interpret this provision using the accepted canons, showing the reasoning.

skills.name: comparative-analyst
skills.description: Compares how a specific legal question is treated across specified jurisdictions or statutes, sourcing each jurisdiction's position only from current authoritative text retrieved this session or supplied by the user — an incomplete comparison with a gap stated plainly is always preferred over a complete-looking one filled from memory. Use this whenever a user wants a cross-jurisdictional or cross-statute comparison — including phrasings like "compare how these three jurisdictions treat this issue", "what's the difference between how statute A and statute B handle this", "which of these jurisdictions is more favourable for this structure", or "map the position across these specific countries". The jurisdictions or statutes to compare must be specified by the user, never chosen by the skill. Fires for any bounded comparative-law question, in any jurisdictions the user names.

interface.short_description: Compare a legal question across named jurisdictions
interface.default_prompt: Use $comparative-analyst to compare how these named jurisdictions treat this specific question.

skills.name: forum-jurisdiction-analyst
skills.description: Analyses which forum and which jurisdiction's law could apply to a dispute, and what actually turns on the choice — substantive law, procedure, remedies, enforcement of judgment — checking any contractual forum-selection or arbitration clause first, and never asserting a jurisdictional rule or a forum's procedural practice from memory. Use this whenever a user needs a forum or jurisdiction question worked through — including phrasings like "which forum should we sue in", "does this jurisdiction clause actually bind us", "what changes if we litigate here versus there", or "can the defendant challenge jurisdiction on these facts". Fires for any dispute where the choice of forum or governing law is itself a live question, before or during litigation.

interface.short_description: Work out which forum, and what turns on the choice
interface.default_prompt: Use $forum-jurisdiction-analyst to work out which forum we should sue in and what actually turns on the choice.

skills.name: issue-spotter
skills.description: Reads a fact pattern and spots every legally relevant issue, potential cause of action, and threshold problem — limitation, standing, jurisdiction, procedural preconditions — comprehensively rather than narrowing to the strongest-looking claim, and flags which deeper-analysis skill each issue needs next rather than analysing any of them in depth itself. Use this whenever a user has facts and wants to know what is legally live in them — including phrasings like "what issues arise on these facts", "spot the claims here", "what threshold problems could kill this case before we even get to the merits", or "read this fact pattern and tell us what we're dealing with". Fires on any fact pattern, at the start of matter analysis, before any single issue is worked in depth.

interface.short_description: Spot issues, causes of action, and threshold problems
interface.default_prompt: Use $issue-spotter to read these facts and spot every issue, cause of action, and threshold problem.

skills.name: legislative-history-analyst
skills.description: Traces how a statutory provision reached its current form — prior versions, amendments, and the reasons for each change — using only sourced material, and keeps an amending act's own stated purpose, a court's later characterisation of that purpose, and this analysis's own inference clearly distinguished as different categories of evidence. Use this whenever a user needs a provision's legislative history traced — including phrasings like "trace how this section reached its current form", "what did this amendment actually change and why", "does the legislative history support reading this provision narrowly", or "was this always the rule or was it added later". Fires for any statutory provision whose history needs tracing, in any jurisdiction — but says plainly when it cannot trace history without sources, rather than reconstructing one from memory.

interface.short_description: Trace how a provision reached its current form
interface.default_prompt: Use $legislative-history-analyst to trace how this provision reached its current form.

skills.name: precedent-mapper
skills.description: Maps the authorities on a specific legal point and how they relate to each other — which follows which, which distinguishes or overrules another, where a genuine split exists — sourcing every case's existence, citation, and holding only from material retrieved this session or supplied by the user. Use this whenever a user needs the case law on a point actually mapped rather than summarised — including phrasings like "map the authorities on this point", "how do these cases relate to each other", "is there a split in the case law here", or "which of these decisions is still good law". Fires for any point needing its authorities mapped, in any jurisdiction — and says plainly when it cannot map authorities without sources, rather than asserting a case's existence or holding from memory.

interface.short_description: Map the authorities on a point and how they relate
interface.default_prompt: Use $precedent-mapper to map the authorities on this point and how they relate to each other.

skills.name: research-synthesiser
skills.description: Weaves research that has already been gathered — from multiple sources, possibly by different people over time, or from other research skills' output — into a single reasoned position on a specific question, surfacing conflicts between sources rather than silently picking a side, flagging gaps rather than filling them, and keeping every step of the reasoning traceable back to the specific supplied material that supports it. Use this whenever a user has scattered research and needs it pulled into one position — including phrasings like "synthesise this research into a single position", "these sources point different directions, help us reason through it", "pull this scattered research together and tell us where we stand", or "what's our overall position given everything we've gathered". Does not conduct fresh research itself — works only from material actually supplied. Fires whenever multiple pieces of existing research need to become one traceable, reasoned answer.

interface.short_description: Weave scattered research into one traceable position
interface.default_prompt: Use $research-synthesiser to pull this scattered research together into a single reasoned position.

skills.name: statutory-interpreter
skills.description: Interprets a specific statutory provision using the recognised canons of interpretation — textual, structural, purposive, and any specific canon whose structural trigger is actually present — checking first whether existing authority already construes the provision, and showing every step of the reasoning rather than asserting a conclusion. Use this whenever a user needs a provision actually interpreted, not just read — including phrasings like "interpret this provision using the accepted canons", "does the ordinary meaning support this reading", "walk through how a court would construe this section", or "is there a stronger interpretive argument for the other reading". Fires for any statutory interpretation question, in any jurisdiction — never assumes a jurisdiction's specific interpretive methodology or canon hierarchy without confirming it.

interface.short_description: Interpret a provision using the accepted canons
interface.default_prompt: Use $statutory-interpreter to interpret this provision using the accepted canons, showing the reasoning.

release.description: Cap table, ESOP, founders' agreement, investment agreement review, SaaS terms, India startup compliance, and term sheet review skills.

interface.short_description: Startup legal workflows
interface.long_description: Seven reusable startup workflows covering cap table dilution modelling, ESOP scheme drafting, founders' agreements, SHA/SSA review, SaaS terms of service, India startup compliance, and term sheet review.
interface.default_prompt: Model the dilution from this new financing round.
default_prompts: Model the dilution from this new financing round.
Review this term sheet for off-market or founder-adverse terms.
Draft a founders' agreement with reverse vesting and IP assignment.

skills.name: cap-table-analyst
skills.description: Works through dilution and ownership on a cap table using only the share counts, valuations, and round terms actually supplied — showing the arithmetic for every calculation and flagging option-pool timing, conversion order, or preference terms that were not specified rather than assuming a standard treatment. Use this whenever a user needs a cap table calculation worked through — including phrasings like "what does this round do to our ownership", "model the dilution from this SAFE conversion", "work out the post-money cap table", "how much does the option pool top-up dilute existing holders", or "run the liquidation waterfall on these preference terms". A quantification tool, not a fairness assessment — it does not judge whether the round terms are good; pair it with term-sheet-reviewer or investment-agreement-reviewer for that. Fires for any priced round, conversion, or waterfall calculation on a startup cap table.

interface.short_description: Work through dilution and ownership on supplied numbers
interface.default_prompt: Use $cap-table-analyst to model what this round does to our ownership and dilution.

skills.name: esop-scheme-drafter
skills.description: Drafts an employee stock option scheme document and individual grant letter template — eligibility, vesting, exercise mechanics, and leaver treatment — using only the parameters actually instructed and flagging tax-advantaged scheme qualification and regulatory approval requirements for verification rather than asserting them. Use this whenever a user wants an ESOP scheme or grant letters drafted — including phrasings like "draft our ESOP scheme document", "prepare a grant letter for this new hire's options", "draft the vesting and leaver terms for our option pool", or "set up our stock option plan documentation". Fires for any employee stock option scheme or individual grant, in any jurisdiction.

interface.short_description: Draft ESOP scheme documents and grant letters
interface.default_prompt: Use $esop-scheme-drafter to draft our ESOP scheme document and a grant letter template.

skills.name: founders-agreement-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a founders' agreement — equity split and roles, reverse vesting of founder equity, IP assignment, decision-making and deadlock provisions, and leaver mechanics — treating an undecided vesting schedule as the single most important open question rather than filling it in with a default. Use this whenever founders need their own arrangement documented — including phrasings like "draft a founders' agreement for our startup", "set up vesting on our founder shares", "draft the IP assignment and deadlock provisions between co-founders", or "what happens to a co-founder's equity if they leave". Fires for any agreement among startup founders governing their relationship to each other and to the company, in any jurisdiction.

interface.short_description: Draft founder agreements: vesting, roles, exit, IP
interface.default_prompt: Use $founders-agreement-drafter to draft a founders' agreement covering vesting, IP assignment, and exit.

skills.name: investment-agreement-reviewer
skills.description: Reviews a shareholders' agreement and share subscription agreement as one interacting system, from the founder's or the investor's side, for control and governance terms, economic terms (liquidation preference, anti-dilution, pre-emption), and exit mechanics (drag-along, tag-along, transfer restrictions) — cross-checked against any term sheet the deal is meant to reflect. Use this whenever a user needs venture financing documents reviewed — including phrasings like "review this SHA from the founder's side", "check this SSA against our term sheet", "what control are we giving away in this shareholders' agreement", "flag anything founder-adverse in this investment round documentation", or "does this liquidation preference actually match what we agreed". Fires for any SHA, SSA, or equivalent venture investment document set, from either side.

interface.short_description: Review SHA/SSA terms from the founder's or investor's side
interface.default_prompt: Use $investment-agreement-reviewer to review this SHA and SSA from the founder's side.

skills.name: saas-terms-drafter
skills.description: Drafts SaaS terms of service or a customer agreement — access grant, service levels, data processing position, IP ownership, limitation of liability, and termination and data-return provisions — flagging data protection applicability, consumer-protection requirements for B2C terms, and liability-cap enforceability for verification rather than asserting them. Use this whenever a user needs terms for a SaaS product — including phrasings like "draft our SaaS terms of service", "prepare a customer agreement for our platform", "what should our data processing position say", "draft terms for a B2C subscription product", or "add termination and data-return provisions to our ToS". Fires for any software-as-a-service or platform terms of service, B2B or B2C, in any jurisdiction.

interface.short_description: Draft SaaS terms of service and customer agreements
interface.default_prompt: Use $saas-terms-drafter to draft our SaaS terms of service for this product.

skills.name: startup-compliance-checker
skills.description: Checks the compliance obligations applicable to a startup given its entity structure, stage, and sector — post-incorporation and structural filings, DPIIT recognition considerations, funding-triggered compliance, and ESOP-related requirements — flagging current specific forms, deadlines, and fees for verification rather than asserting them from memory. Use this whenever a user needs a startup's compliance position checked — including phrasings like "what compliance do we need at our stage", "check our post-funding filing obligations", "does raising this round trigger any FEMA reporting", "what does DPIIT recognition actually require of us", or "build a compliance checklist for our current stage". India-specific. Fires for any private limited company or LLP startup checking its obligations by stage.

interface.short_description: Check India startup compliance by stage and structure
interface.default_prompt: Use $startup-compliance-checker to check our compliance obligations at our current stage and structure.

skills.name: term-sheet-reviewer
skills.description: Reviews a venture financing term sheet before definitive documents are drafted, flagging terms that are commonly considered off-market or adverse to the reviewed side — always framed as the reviewer's own general commercial understanding requiring the user's own confirmation against current market data, never asserted as settled fact. Use this whenever a user has received or is negotiating a term sheet — including phrasings like "review this term sheet before we sign", "flag anything off-market in these terms", "is this anti-dilution provision unusual", "check this term sheet for founder-adverse clauses", or "what's missing from this term sheet for our stage". Distinct from investment-agreement-reviewer, which reviews the definitive SHA/SSA — this works from the shorter, earlier-stage document. Fires for any term sheet, letter of intent, or heads of terms for a venture financing round, from either side.

interface.short_description: Flag off-market and founder-adverse term sheet terms
interface.default_prompt: Use $term-sheet-reviewer to review this term sheet and flag anything off-market or founder-adverse.

release.description: FEMA, GST, tax appeal and assessment-reply, tax opinion, transfer pricing, and treaty-analysis skills.

interface.short_description: Tax law workflows
interface.long_description: Seven reusable tax workflows covering FEMA analysis, GST compliance, tax appeal grounds, assessment replies, formal tax opinions, transfer pricing documentation, and treaty entitlement analysis.
interface.default_prompt: What's the GST treatment of this supply?
default_prompts: What's the GST treatment of this supply?
Draft grounds of appeal against this tax assessment order.
Analyse our treaty entitlement on this cross-border royalty payment.

skills.name: fema-analyst
skills.description: Analyses a cross-border transaction against India's foreign exchange control framework — transaction classification, residential status under FEMA, applicable route, pricing guideline and reporting requirements — flagging current sectoral caps and form requirements for verification rather than asserting them from memory. Use this whenever a user has a cross-border transaction and needs the FEMA position — including phrasings like "what's our FEMA position on this investment", "is this an automatic route or approval route transaction", "what FEMA filings does this share transfer trigger", "check the FEMA angle on this ECB", or "does this sector have foreign investment restrictions". India-specific. Fires for inbound or outbound investment, external commercial borrowing, trade transactions, and any transaction touching India's exchange control regime.

interface.short_description: Work out the FEMA position on a cross-border transaction
interface.default_prompt: Use $fema-analyst to work out our FEMA position on this cross-border investment.

skills.name: gst-compliance-analyst
skills.description: Analyses a supply for its GST treatment — classification as goods or services, place and time of supply, applicable rate, reverse charge, input tax credit eligibility, and registration and compliance obligations — flagging current rate notifications and thresholds for verification rather than asserting them from memory. Use this whenever a user needs the GST position on a transaction — including phrasings like "what's the GST treatment of this supply", "does reverse charge apply here", "can we claim input tax credit on this", "do we need to register for GST because of this transaction", or "check the place of supply on this cross-state contract". India-specific. Fires for any supply of goods or services, or a composite or mixed supply, under India's GST regime.

interface.short_description: Check GST treatment and compliance obligations
interface.default_prompt: Use $gst-compliance-analyst to check the GST treatment of this supply and our compliance obligations.

skills.name: tax-appeal-grounds-drafter
skills.description: Drafts grounds of appeal against an already-passed tax assessment or order — each ground tied to a specific part of the order, factual and legal grounds kept distinct, and procedural grounds such as limitation or natural justice raised prominently. Use this whenever a user wants to appeal a tax order — including phrasings like "draft grounds of appeal against this assessment order", "we want to challenge this GST demand order", "prepare an appeal against this disallowance", "draft the grounds for the tribunal", or "challenge this order for lack of a hearing". India-specific. Distinct from tax-assessment-reply-drafter, which responds before an order is passed — this challenges one that already has been. Fires for any appeal against an income tax, GST, or other tax assessment or order, at any appellate forum.

interface.short_description: Draft grounds of appeal against a tax order
interface.default_prompt: Use $tax-appeal-grounds-drafter to draft grounds of appeal against this assessment order.

skills.name: tax-assessment-reply-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a reply to a tax assessment or scrutiny notice — before any order has been passed — addressing every query raised, referencing the client's actual supporting documents, and flagging the response deadline and any procedural defect in the notice itself. Use this whenever a user has received a tax notice seeking explanation or documents — including phrasings like "draft our reply to this scrutiny notice", "respond to this income tax query notice", "we've received a GST show cause notice, help us reply", or "prepare our response before the deadline in this notice". India-specific. Distinct from tax-appeal-grounds-drafter, which challenges an order that has already been passed — this responds while the proceeding is still open. Fires for any pre-order tax notice, income tax or GST, seeking explanation, documents, or a response.

interface.short_description: Reply to tax assessment and scrutiny notices
interface.default_prompt: Use $tax-assessment-reply-drafter to draft our reply to this scrutiny notice before the deadline.

skills.name: tax-opinion-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a formal written tax opinion — question, facts, analysis, conclusion — and, distinctly from a general legal opinion, states the risk profile of the position taken, not just its legal conclusion. Use this whenever a user wants a reasoned written position on a tax question — including phrasings like "write a tax opinion on whether this deduction is available", "what's our position on this structuring, with the risk stated", "prepare an opinion on the withholding treatment of this payment", or "I need a written tax position we can rely on, with the risk graded". Jurisdiction-neutral — never assumes which tax law applies. Shares its rigor with legal-opinion-drafter but adds the risk-characterisation step specific to tax positions. Fires for any formal tax opinion request, in any jurisdiction.

interface.short_description: Draft tax opinions with the position and risk stated
interface.default_prompt: Use $tax-opinion-drafter to draft a tax opinion on this position, with the risk graded alongside the legal conclusion.

skills.name: transfer-pricing-documenter
skills.description: Documents an intercompany transaction for transfer pricing purposes — functional analysis (functions, assets, risks), method selection reasoned from that analysis, and a benchmarking record built only from comparables actually supplied — flagging jurisdiction-specific documentation thresholds and method hierarchy rules for verification. Use this whenever a user needs a related-party transaction documented or benchmarked — including phrasings like "document this intercompany service arrangement for transfer pricing", "which method fits this royalty arrangement", "build the FAR analysis for this distribution structure", or "check whether this margin falls within an arm's length range on these comparables". Jurisdiction-neutral — never assumes a specific transfer pricing regime applies. Fires for any related-party or intercompany transaction requiring transfer pricing documentation, in any jurisdiction.

interface.short_description: Document intercompany transactions and benchmarking
interface.default_prompt: Use $transfer-pricing-documenter to document this intercompany transaction, with a functional analysis and benchmarking record.

skills.name: treaty-analyst
skills.description: Analyses treaty entitlement and relief on given facts — treaty residency, the applicable income article, beneficial ownership and limitation-of-benefits conditions, and the relief potentially available — flagging every substantive term for verification against the actual treaty text rather than assuming a generic model convention applies. Use this whenever a user needs the double tax treaty position on a cross-border payment or transaction — including phrasings like "are we entitled to treaty relief on this royalty payment", "what's the withholding position under this DTAA", "check our treaty residency here", "does this payment qualify for the reduced treaty rate", or "walk through the limitation of benefits test on these facts". Jurisdiction-neutral — never assumes which two countries' treaty applies or what it says. Fires for any cross-border payment or transaction where treaty relief is in question.

interface.short_description: Analyse treaty entitlement and relief on given facts
interface.default_prompt: Use $treaty-analyst to analyse our treaty entitlement and relief on this cross-border payment.

release.description: Adversarial review, assumption flagging, citation integrity checking, and cross-document consistency skills — a quality-control pass for a finished draft from any practice area.

interface.short_description: Legal quality-control checks
interface.long_description: Four reusable quality-control workflows: attacking a draft the way opposing counsel would, surfacing every assumption it depends on, checking every citation for integrity, and cross-checking a document set for internal consistency.
interface.default_prompt: Attack this draft the way opposing counsel would before we send it.
default_prompts: Attack this draft the way opposing counsel would before we send it.
Surface every assumption this opinion depends on.
Check every citation in this document for integrity.

skills.name: adversarial-reviewer
skills.description: Attacks a finished draft the way opposing counsel, a skeptical judge, or a regulator would — hunting for exploitable ambiguity, gaps, internal inconsistency, and unsupported assertions, and writing out the strongest counter-argument to the document's own conclusions. Use this as a final stress test before a document goes out — including phrasings like "attack this draft before we send it", "what would opposing counsel do with this", "poke holes in this opinion", "find the weakest point in this pleading", or "red-team this before we file it". It finds problems; it does not fix them — hand off to the relevant drafting or redline skill for that. Fires on any finished draft in any practice area — contracts, pleadings, opinions, notices.

interface.short_description: Attack a draft the way opposing counsel would
interface.default_prompt: Use $adversarial-reviewer to attack this draft the way opposing counsel would before we send it.

skills.name: assumption-flagger
skills.description: Surfaces every assumption a draft depends on — factual, legal, definitional, about another party's future conduct, or about scope — whether the document states them or not, so they can be verified or challenged before anyone relies on it. Use this as an independent audit pass on any document — including phrasings like "what is this opinion actually assuming", "surface every assumption in this risk assessment", "what would have to be true for this conclusion to hold", "audit this draft for unstated premises", or "check what this document is taking for granted". Works on documents from any source, not just this practice pack's own outputs — an opinion received from other counsel, a judgment, an external draft. Fires on any document whose conclusions rest on premises worth checking before relying on it.

interface.short_description: Surface every assumption a draft depends on
interface.default_prompt: Use $assumption-flagger to surface every assumption this draft depends on.

skills.name: citation-integrity-checker
skills.description: Extracts every citation in a document — statute, case, rule, regulation, quotation, or cross-reference — and states exactly what needs verifying about it and how, attempting live verification where research tools are available this session and producing a structured checklist where they are not. Use this whenever a document's citations need checking before anyone relies on them — including phrasings like "check every citation in this opinion before we send it", "verify these case references are real", "does this quote actually say what we're attributing to it", "audit the citations in this pleading", or "make sure none of these sections are made up". Directly responsive to the risk this whole practice pack warns about — an AI-assisted draft can produce a citation that looks correct and is not. Fires on any document containing legal citations, quotations, or cross-references, in any practice area.

interface.short_description: Check every citation for integrity before relying on it
interface.default_prompt: Use $citation-integrity-checker to check every citation in this document before we rely on it.

skills.name: consistency-checker
skills.description: Checks a document or a set of documents for internal consistency — the same fact stated the same way everywhere, dates that don't contradict each other, defined terms used consistently, and figures that match across every mention — and flags every discrepancy found without silently resolving which version is correct. Use this whenever a document set needs a consistency audit — including phrasings like "check these documents for consistency before we file them", "do the dates in this bundle actually line up", "make sure this defined term is used the same way throughout", "check the figures in this agreement match the schedule", or "cross-check this document set for contradictions". Distinct from citation-integrity-checker, which is about external authority, and assumption-flagger, which is about unstated premises — this is about internal self-consistency of what is actually stated. Fires on any single long document or document set, in any practice area.

interface.short_description: Check facts, dates, and figures across a document set
interface.default_prompt: Use $consistency-checker to check these documents for consistency before we file them.

interface.short_description: Read-only technical advice

Codex Advisor automatically adds a fresh, read-only second opinion when Codex identifies a material technical decision.

Standard remains Terra/high for ordinary bounded architecture, interface, data-model, and generic-advisor decisions. Specialist remains GPT-6 Sol/high only when targeted evidence still leaves a cross-system design, compatibility or concurrency boundary, competing diagnosis, security or trust boundary, recovery, irreversible migration, or data-loss decision unresolved. Project importance, security adjacency, or an ordinary architecture question alone stays Standard. A separate advisor-astra role offers explicit-only Astra/high consultation for the most complex uses; it is never selected automatically, uses more Codex allowance, and remains subject to account and runtime availability.

Every consultation runs in a separate read-only, tool-free process. It cannot change your files, run commands, browse the web, or make decisions for you. You remain in control: Advisor does not implement, deploy, or perform final review.

release.description: Give your AI assistant the right data to answer questions about your business.

interface.short_description: Analyze your business data
interface.long_description:
Motley gives your AI assistant the right data to answer questions about your business.

Motley connects to your company's data sources and keeps a semantic layer: the definitions of your metrics, your tables, and how they relate. When you ask a question, such as "What was revenue by store last quarter?", your assistant uses Motley to find the right tables and metrics, runs the query, and answers with the numbers and the query behind them. You can check how each number was calculated. Everyone in your organization works from the same definitions.

What you can do:
- Ask questions about your business metrics, trends, and breakdowns.
- Give context, such as what "active customer" means, so that later answers use it.
- Set up and improve the semantic layer for a connected data source.

What you need: a Motley account. Every account includes a demo data source. To connect your own data, contact the Motley team.

Limitations: Motley reads only the data sources that your organization connects. It does not search the web and does not change the data in your databases. Large raw extracts are truncated, so ask for aggregated results. Changes to the semantic layer need the editor role.

release.description: Publish the app your agent just built to your team: a private address behind sign-in, with a database, scheduled jobs and email. No servers to set up.

interface.short_description: Publish apps to your team
interface.long_description:
Spryloom publishes the app you just built so your coworkers can use it, behind sign-in. Say "share this with my team" and the agent writes a small manifest, runs `spry publish`, and gives you a private address. Spryloom builds the app, gives it its own database if it needs one, and runs scheduled jobs and email when the app declares them. Coworkers you invite sign in with an emailed link; nobody else can open it.

The skill also guides the agent while it builds, so the app reads its port and settings from the environment, keeps data in Postgres and publishes the first time.

Who it's for: anyone building internal tools, dashboards, reports or small team apps with an agent, who wants them used by their team without setting up hosting, a database or sign-in.

Limitations: the skill uses the `spry` command line (the npm package `spryloom`), which needs Node.js 20.19 or later and network access. Signing in is a one-time emailed link that you approve yourself. Apps run Node.js or are static pages. File uploads aren't supported yet, and an app can reach only the outside services on Spryloom's list.

release.description: A conversational CFD companion for solver choice, case setup, mesh review, computation, and result interpretation.

interface.short_description: CFD modeling and simulation
interface.long_description:
CFDAgent helps researchers and engineers work through computational fluid dynamics and fluid-mechanics problems in conversation. Discuss the physics, compare suitable solvers and their preparation and compute costs, set up cases, review mesh quality, plan runs, examine results, and prepare reproducible postprocessing and reports.

The plugin provides concise guidance and references that the host loads as needed. It follows the current task and evidence rather than a fixed sequence. Working notes help continue an existing project, and exported figures are inspected for readability.

References cover OpenFOAM, SU2, FDS, MFiX, DualSPHysics, code_saturne, Basilisk, Nek5000/nekRS, Palabos, OpenLB, Nektar++, PyFR, and PyIB. Solver choice depends on the problem and available evidence.

Actual simulations require host tools that can access the project and execute commands, a suitable solver, and the necessary compute environment. The plugin does not bundle solvers, provide a hosted computation service, or require an MCP server. Available execution features depend on the host and the user's environment.

Developed by Zhaoyue Xu, Experimental Zoology Group, Wageningen University & Research (WUR), Netherlands.

interface.short_description: Preset workflows via sup CLI
interface.long_description:
Preset CLI Skills teaches coding agents a repeatable way to drive Preset and Apache Superset from the `sup` command line tool (PyPI package `superset-sup`). Use it for shell one-liners, batch asset exports, ad-hoc SQL, and CI/CD automation against a Preset workspace.

The package contains two skills. `preset-cli` covers the non-destructive foundation: installing and authenticating the CLI, selecting a workspace, choosing an output format, running read-only queries, and exporting charts, dashboards, and datasets as YAML. `preset-cli-mutations` covers state-changing work, including pushing asset YAML, destructive flags such as `--force` and `--overwrite`, and cross-workspace `sync`. It requires a dry run or preview plus an explicit confirmation before any write, and it keeps credentials out of command output.

Intended for data engineers, analytics engineers, and platform teams who already manage Preset or Apache Superset assets as code.

Limitations: the skills assume the `sup` CLI is installed and authenticated in the execution environment, and they act only on workspaces the signed-in user can already reach. They do not bundle credentials, and they do not create or administer Preset accounts.

release.description: Build iOS apps with workflows for App Intents, SwiftUI UI work, Simulator mirroring in the Codex in-app browser, performance profiling, leak investigation, and simulator debugging.

interface.short_description: Build, refine, and debug iOS apps with App Intents, SwiftUI, and Xcode workflows
interface.long_description: Use Build iOS Apps to design App Intents and App Shortcuts, build or refactor SwiftUI UI, render SwiftUI previews in the Codex in-app browser, adopt modern iOS patterns such as Liquid Glass, audit runtime performance, capture ETTrace profiles, investigate memory leaks, and debug apps on simulators with XcodeBuildMCP-backed workflows.
interface.default_prompt: Build or debug an iOS app with SwiftUI, App Intents, and Simulator.
default_prompts: Build or debug an iOS app with SwiftUI, App Intents, and Simulator.

skills.name: ios-app-intents
skills.description: Design App Intents, app entities, and App Shortcuts for iOS system surfaces. Use when exposing app actions or content to Shortcuts, Siri, Spotlight, widgets, or controls.

interface.short_description: Build and debug iOS App Intents integrations

skills.name: ios-debugger-agent
skills.description: Build, run, and debug iOS apps on Simulator with XcodeBuildMCP. Use when launching an app, inspecting simulator UI or logs, or diagnosing runtime behavior.

interface.short_description: Debug iOS apps on Simulator
interface.default_prompt: Use $ios-debugger-agent to build, launch, and inspect the current iOS app on the booted simulator.

skills.name: ios-ettrace-performance
skills.description: Capture and interpret iOS Simulator ETTrace profiles. Use when profiling launch or runtime latency, comparing traces, or finding CPU-heavy stacks.

interface.short_description: Profile symbolicated iOS simulator flows with ETTrace
interface.default_prompt: Use $ios-ettrace-performance to capture a focused iOS simulator ETTrace profile and identify time-heavy stacks.

skills.name: ios-memgraph-leaks
skills.description: Capture and inspect iOS leaks and memgraphs. Use when debugging leaked objects, retain cycles, memory growth, or before/after leak evidence.

interface.short_description: Capture and prove iOS simulator memory leaks
interface.default_prompt: Use $ios-memgraph-leaks to capture an iOS simulator memgraph, identify retention paths, and verify leak fixes.

skills.name: ios-simulator-browser
skills.description: Mirror an iOS Simulator into the Codex in-app browser and render SwiftUI previews from importable Swift packages in that simulator with hot reload. Use when a user wants to watch or interact with an iOS app in the browser, see a SwiftUI preview outside Xcode Canvas, iterate live on a preview, or capture browser-visible simulator proof.

interface.short_description: Mirror iOS Simulator
interface.default_prompt: Use $ios-simulator-browser to render a SwiftUI preview in the in-app browser.

skills.name: swiftui-liquid-glass
skills.description: Implement and review iOS 26+ SwiftUI Liquid Glass UI. Use when adopting Liquid Glass or checking its correctness, performance, and design fit.

interface.short_description: Build SwiftUI Liquid Glass features
interface.default_prompt: Use $swiftui-liquid-glass to implement or review a SwiftUI feature using Liquid Glass APIs.

skills.name: swiftui-performance-audit
skills.description: Audit SwiftUI runtime performance from code first. Use when diagnosing slow rendering, janky scrolling, expensive updates, or profiling needs.

interface.short_description: Audit SwiftUI runtime performance
interface.default_prompt: Use $swiftui-performance-audit to review this SwiftUI code for performance issues and suggest concrete fixes.

skills.name: swiftui-ui-patterns

interface.short_description: Apply practical SwiftUI UI patterns
